knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
Suppose that the assertion is false. Then there exists a time \( \tau  \in \; \left( {0,{t}_{0}}\right) \) with the property that the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) does not split off a line. Since \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC, we conclude that \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is locally irreducible. In view of Berger's holonomy classification theorem, there are four possible cases:

Case 1: Suppose first that \( {\operatorname{Hol}}^{0}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = {SO}\left( n\right) \) . If we fix an arbitrary pair of real numbers \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) , then Theorem 9.13 in [5] implies that the set of all orthonormal four-frames \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) satisfying

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {\mu }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda \mu }{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  = 0
\]

is invariant under parallel transport. Since \( {\operatorname{Hol}}^{0}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = {SO}\left( n\right) \) , we conclude that

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {\mu }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda \mu }{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  > 0
\]

for all orthonormal four-frames \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) and all \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . In other words, the curvature tensor of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) lies in the interior of the PIC2 cone.

Let \( \Omega \) be a bounded open neighborhood of the point \( {p}_{0} \) with smooth boundary. Let us choose a smooth function \( f : \bar{\Omega } \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) with the property that \( f > 0 \) in \( \Omega , f = 0 \) on \( \partial \Omega \) , and \( {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) } - \frac{1}{2}f \) id \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC2. Let \( F \) : \( \bar{\Omega } \times  \left\lbrack  {\tau ,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) denote the solution of the linear heat equation with respect to the evolving metric \( g\left( t\right) \) with initial data \( F\left( {\cdot ,\tau }\right)  = f \) and Dirichlet boundary condition \( F = 0 \) on \( \partial \Omega  \times  \left\lbrack  {\tau ,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . Let \( S \mathrel{\text{ := }} {R}_{g\left( t\right) } - \frac{1}{2}F\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) id \( \oslash \) id. Then \( {D}_{t}S = {\Delta S} + Q\left( S\right)  + {2F}\operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{id} + \left( {n - 1}\right) {F}^{2}\operatorname{id} \oslash  \operatorname{id} \) . Using the maximum principle, we conclude that \( {R}_{g\left( t\right) } - \frac{1}{2}F\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) id \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC2 at each point in \( \Omega  \times  \left\lbrack  {\tau ,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . Since \( F\left( {{p}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  > 0 \) , the curvature tensor at \( \left( {{p}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) lies in the interior of the PIC2 cone, contrary to our assumption.

Case 2: Suppose that \( n = {2m} \) and \( {\operatorname{Hol}}^{0}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = U\left( m\right) \) . In this case, the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is a Kähler manifold. This is impossible since \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC.

Case 3: Suppose next that \( n = {4m} \geq  8 \) and \( {\operatorname{Hol}}^{0}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = \operatorname{Sp}\left( m\right) \) . \( \mathrm{{Sp}}\left( 1\right) \) . In this case, the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is a quaternionic Kähler manifold. In particular, \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is an Einstein manifold. Since \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC, we conclude that the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is a round sphere (cf. [4]). This is impossible.

Case 4: Suppose finally that \( {\operatorname{Hol}}^{0}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  \neq  {SO}\left( n\right) \) and \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is locally symmetric. In this case, \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is an Einstein manifold, for otherwise the eigenspaces of the Ricci tensor give a splitting of the tangent bundle into parallel subbundles, which is impossible since \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is locally irreducible. Since \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC, it follows that the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is a round sphere (cf. [4]). This contradicts the fact that \( {\operatorname{Hol}}^{0}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  \neq  {SO}\left( n\right) \) . This completes the proof of Theorem 6.6.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) , is a complete ancient solution to the Ricci flow that is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales, is weakly PIC2, and satisfies \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \varnothing \) id \( \in \) PIC for some uniform constant \( \theta  > 0 \) . Moreover, suppose that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies the Harnack inequality

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\operatorname{scal} + 2\langle \nabla \operatorname{scal}, v\rangle  + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {v, v}\right)  \geq  0
\]

for every tangent vector \( v \) . Then \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) has bounded curvature.

knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
Since \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies the Harnack inequality, it suffices to show that \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) has bounded curvature. The proof is by contradiction. Suppose that \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) has unbounded curvature.

By the strict maximum principle, we can find a real number \( \delta  > 0 \) with the property that the scalar curvature \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is strictly positive for \( t \in  ( - \delta ,0\rbrack \) .

Consequently, \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC for \( t \in  ( - \delta ,0\rbrack \) . We distinguish two cases:

Case 1: Suppose first that \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC2. In this case, \( M \) is diffeomorphic to \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) by the soul theorem (cf. [10]). By a standard point-picking argument, there exists a sequence of points \( {x}_{j} \in  M \) such that \( {Q}_{j} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \; \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right)  \geq  {j}^{4} \) and

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j},{2j}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  4{Q}_{j}.
\]

Since \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies the Harnack inequality, we obtain

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j},{2j}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-4{j}^{2}{Q}_{j}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack  }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  4{Q}_{j}.
\]

Using Shi's interior derivative estimate, we obtain bounds for all the derivatives of curvature on \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j}, j{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-{j}^{2}{Q}_{j}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) . We now dilate the flow \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) around the point \( \left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) \) by the factor \( {Q}_{j} \) . Using the noncollapsing assumption and the curvature derivative estimates, we conclude that, after passing to a subsequence, the rescaled flows converge in the Cheeger-Gromov sense to a smooth nonflat ancient solution \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) . The limit \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is complete, has bounded curvature, is weakly PIC2, and satisfies \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} \in \) PIC. By Proposition 6.8, the manifold \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) splits off a line. By Corollary 6.7, universal cover of \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a family of shrinking cylinders \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) . Therefore, \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a quotient \( \left( {{S}^{n - 1}/\Gamma }\right)  \times  \mathbb{R} \) . If \( \Gamma \) is nontrivial, then a result of Hamilton implies that \( M \) contains a nontrivial incompressible \( \left( {n - 1}\right) \) -dimensional space form \( {S}^{n - 1}/\Gamma \) (cf. [6, Th. A.2]), but this is impossible since \( M \) is diffeomorphic to \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . Thus, \( \Gamma \) is trivial, and \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a standard cylinder \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) . Consequently, \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) contains a sequence of necks with radii converging to 0 . This contradicts Proposition 6.9.

Case 2: Suppose finally that \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is not strictly PIC2. By Proposition 6.6, the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a product \( \left( {X,{g}_{X}\left( t\right) }\right)  \times  \mathbb{R} \) for each \( t \in  ( - \delta ,0\rbrack \) . Clearly, \( \left( {X,{g}_{X}\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  ( - \delta ,0\rbrack \) , is a complete solution to the Ricci flow of dimension \( n - 1 \) , which is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales, weakly PIC2, and uniformly PIC1. By assumption, \( \left( {X,{g}_{X}\left( 0\right) }\right) \) has unbounded curvature. Using a point-picking lemma, we can construct a sequence of points \( {x}_{j} \in  X \) such that \( {Q}_{j} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right)  \geq  {j}^{4} \) and

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{{g}_{X}\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j},{2j}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  4{Q}_{j}.
\]

As in Case 1, the Harnack inequality and Shi's interior derivative estimate give bounds for all the derivatives of curvature on \( {B}_{{g}_{X}\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j}, j{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-{j}^{2}{Q}_{j}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) . We now dilate the manifold \( \left( {X,{g}_{X}\left( 0\right) }\right) \) around the point \( {x}_{j} \) by the factor \( {Q}_{j} \) . Passing to the limit as \( j \rightarrow  \infty \) , we obtain a smooth nonflat limit that is uniformly PIC1 and that must split off a line by Proposition 6.8. This is a contradiction.

We begin with an elementary lemma:

Lemma 3.3. Let \( n \geq  {12} \) , let \( 0 < b \leq  {b}_{\max } \) , and let a and \( \omega \) be defined as above. Then

\[
2 + \left( {n - 8}\right) b - 2\left( {n + 2}\right) \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - n{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}{b}^{3} > 0
\]

and

\[
\left( {\frac{n - 2}{n - 3} + \frac{2\left( {n - 2}\right) }{n}\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right)  + 8\left( {n - 3}\right) {b}^{2}}\right) \left( {\frac{n - 2}{n - 3} + 2\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) }\right)  \leq  \frac{\omega }{2}.
\]

Proof. Note that \( 2 - 2\left( {n + 2}\right) \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} \geq  0 \) and \( \left( {n - 8}\right) b - n{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}{b}^{3} \geq  0 \) . If we add these inequalities, the first statement follows.

To prove the second statement, we observe that

\[
\frac{2 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}{{\left( 2 + \left( n - 3\right) b\right) }^{2}} \geq  \frac{1}{2 + {nb}} \geq  \frac{4}{9}.
\]

This implies

\[
\omega  = {\left( 1 - 4\left( n - 2\right) {b}^{2}\right) }^{2}\left( {\frac{1}{nb} + \frac{n - 2}{n}}\right) \sqrt{\frac{27}{8}\frac{2 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}{{\left( 2 + \left( n - 3\right) b\right) }^{2}}}
\]

\[
\geq  {\left( 1 - \frac{n - 2}{4{n}^{2}}\right) }^{2}\frac{{5n} - 2}{n}\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}.
\]

On the other hand, we have \( a = \frac{{\left( 2 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{2\left( {2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right) }b \leq  \frac{2 + {nb}}{2}b \leq  \frac{9}{8}b \) . This implies \( {2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a \leq  {na} \leq  \frac{9n}{8}b \leq  \frac{9}{32} \) , which gives

\[
\frac{n - 2}{n - 3} + \frac{2\left( {n - 2}\right) }{n}\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right)  + 8\left( {n - 3}\right) {b}^{2} \leq  \frac{n - 2}{n - 3} + \frac{9\left( {n - 2}\right) }{16n} + \frac{n - 3}{2{n}^{2}}
\]

and

\[
\frac{n - 2}{n - 3} + 2\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right)  \leq  \frac{n - 2}{n - 3} + \frac{9}{16}.
\]

It is elementary to verify that

\[
\left( {\frac{n - 2}{n - 3} + \frac{9\left( {n - 2}\right) }{16n} + \frac{n - 3}{2{n}^{2}}}\right) \left( {\frac{n - 2}{n - 3} + \frac{9}{16}}\right)  \leq  {\left( 1 - \frac{n - 2}{4{n}^{2}}\right) }^{2}\frac{{5n} - 2}{n}\sqrt{\frac{3}{8}}
\]

for \( n \geq  {12} \) . This proves the assertion.

LEMMA 3.4. Let \( 0 < b \leq  {b}_{\max } \) , and let a be defined as above. Then

\[
\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - {2a}}\right) {xy} + {2a}\left( {x + 2}\right) \left( {y + 2}\right)  + {b}^{2}\left( {{x}^{2} + {y}^{2}}\right)  \geq  0
\]

whenever \( x, y \geq   - \frac{2\left( {2 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) }{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b} \) .

Proof. Let \( D = \left\{  {\left( {x, y}\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{2} : x, y \geq   - \frac{2\left( {2 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) }{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}}\right\} \) , and define \( \psi  : D \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) by \( \psi \left( {x, y}\right)  = \left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - {2a}}\right) {xy} + {2a}\left( {x + 2}\right) \left( {y + 2}\right)  + {b}^{2}\left( {{x}^{2} + {y}^{2}}\right) \) . Clearly, \( \psi \left( {x, y}\right)  \rightarrow  \infty \) as \( \left( {x, y}\right)  \in  D \) approaches infinity. Hence, there exists a point in \( D \) where \( \psi \) attains its minimum. The Hessian of \( \psi \) is given by

\[
\left\lbrack  \begin{matrix} 2{b}^{2} & {2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} \\  {2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} & 2{b}^{2} \end{matrix}\right\rbrack  .
\]

Since the Hessian of \( \psi \) has two eigenvalues of opposite signs, the function \( \psi \) attains its minimum on the boundary of \( D \) . On the other hand, a straightforward calculation gives

\[
\psi \left( {-\frac{2\left( {2 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) }{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}, y}\right)  = {b}^{2}{y}^{2} \geq  0.
\]

Thus, \( \psi  \geq  0 \) on \( \partial D \) . This implies \( \psi  \geq  0 \) on \( D \) .

Lemma 3.5. Suppose that \( S \in  \mathcal{E}\left( b\right) \) . Then \( \left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - {2a}}\right) \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\left( S\right) \varnothing \; \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  + {2a}\operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  + 2{b}^{2}\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }^{2} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} \in \) PIC.

Proof. Let

\[
U \mathrel{\text{ := }} \left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - {2a}}\right) \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\left( S\right)  \oslash  \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\left( S\right)  + {2a}\operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  + 2{b}^{2}\mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }{\left( S\right) }^{2} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}.
\]

Let \( \zeta ,\eta  \in  {\mathbb{C}}^{n} \) be linearly independent vectors satisfying \( g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right)  = g\left( {\zeta ,\eta }\right)  = \; g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right)  = 0 \) . We claim that \( U\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  \geq  0 \) . We can find vectors \( z, w \in \; \operatorname{span}\{ \zeta ,\eta \} \) such that \( g\left( {z,\bar{z}}\right)  = g\left( {w,\bar{w}}\right)  = 2, g\left( {z,\bar{w}}\right)  = 0 \) , and \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \left( {z,\bar{w}}\right)  = 0 \) . The identities \( g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right)  = g\left( {\zeta ,\eta }\right)  = g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right)  = 0 \) give \( g\left( {z, z}\right)  = g\left( {z, w}\right)  = g\left( {w, w}\right) \; = 0 \) . Consequently, we may write \( z = {e}_{1} + i{e}_{2} \) and \( w = {e}_{3} + i{e}_{4} \) for some orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\}   \subset  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . Using the identity \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \left( {z,\bar{w}}\right)  = 0 \) , we obtain

\[
U\left( {z, w,\bar{z},\bar{w}}\right)
\]

\[
= 2\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - {2a}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{33} + {\operatorname{Ric}}_{44}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {4a}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{33} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{44}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 4{b}^{2}\left( {{\left( \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }{\left( S\right) }^{2}\right) }_{11} + {\left( \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }{\left( S\right) }^{2}\right) }_{22} + {\left( \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }{\left( S\right) }^{2}\right) }_{33} + {\left( \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }{\left( S\right) }^{2}\right) }_{44}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  2\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - {2a}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{33} + {\operatorname{Ric}}_{44}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {4a}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{33} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{44}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{b}^{2}\left( {{\left( \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{\mathrm{o}}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{\mathrm{o}}{\left( S\right) }_{22}\right) }^{2} + {\left( \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{\mathrm{o}}{\left( S\right) }_{33} + \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{\mathrm{o}}{\left( S\right) }_{44}\right) }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{2\operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{2}}{{n}^{2}}\left\lbrack  {\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - {2a}}\right) {xy} + {2a}\left( {x + 2}\right) \left( {y + 2}\right)  + {b}^{2}\left( {{x}^{2} + {y}^{2}}\right) }\right\rbrack  ,
\]

where \( x \) and \( y \) are defined by \( x \mathrel{\text{ := }} \frac{n}{\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }\left( {{\operatorname{Ric}}_{S}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + {\operatorname{Ric}}_{S}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right) \) and \( y \mathrel{\text{ := }} \; \frac{n}{\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }\left( {{\mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }}_{3}{\left( S\right) }_{33} + {\mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }}_{3}{\left( S\right) }_{44}}\right) \) . Condition (iii) implies that \( x, y \geq   - {2\gamma } - 2 = \; - \frac{2\left( {2 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) }{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b} \) . Using Lemma 3.4, we obtain \( U\left( {z, w,\bar{z},\bar{w}}\right)  \geq  0 \) . Since \( \operatorname{span}\{ \zeta ,\eta \} \; = \operatorname{span}\{ z, w\} \) , it follows that \( U\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  \geq  0 \) . Thus, \( U \in \) PIC, as claimed.

LemMA 3.6. Suppose that \( S \in  \mathcal{E}\left( b\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) . Then \( {D}_{a, b}\left( S\right) \) lies in the interior of the PIC cone.

Proof. If \( {\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\left( S\right) \right| }^{2} = 0 \) , the assertion is trivial. If \( {\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\left( S\right) \right| }^{2} > 0 \) , the assertion follows from Lemma 3.5, taking into account the fact that

\[
n{b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right)  - 2\left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b} + n{b}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{{b}^{2}}{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\left( {2 + \left( {n - 8}\right) b - 2\left( {n + 2}\right) \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - n{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}{b}^{3}}\right)  > 0
\]

for \( 0 < b \leq  {b}_{\max } \) .

After these preparations, we now give the proof of Theorem 3.2. It suffices to show that the cone \( \mathcal{E}\left( b\right) \) is transversally invariant under the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}S = \; Q\left( S\right)  + {D}_{a, b}\left( S\right) \) for each \( 0 < b \leq  {b}_{\max } \) . By Lemma 3.6, we can find a small positive number \( \varepsilon \) (depending on \( b \) ) such that \( {D}_{a, b}\left( S\right)  - {2\varepsilon }\operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} \in \) PIC for all \( S \in  \mathcal{E}\left( b\right) \) . We evolve \( T \) by the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}T = {S}^{2} + \varepsilon \operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{2} \) id \( \oslash \) id.

Lemma 3.7. Suppose that \( S \in  \mathcal{E}\left( b\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} , T \geq  0 \) , and \( S - T \in \) PIC. Then \( \frac{d}{dt}T > 0. \)

Proof. This follows immediately from the evolution equation for \( T \) .

LEMMA 3.8. Suppose that \( S \in  \mathcal{E}\left( b\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} , T \geq  0 \) , and \( S - T \in \) PIC. Then \( \frac{d}{dt}\left( {S - T}\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{S - T} \) PIC.

Proof. We compute \( \frac{d}{dt}\left( {S - T}\right)  = {S}^{\# } + {D}_{a, b}\left( S\right)  - \varepsilon \operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{2} \) id/oid. Applying Proposition A.9 with \( U \mathrel{\text{ := }} S - T \) , we conclude that \( {S}^{\# } \in  {T}_{S - T} \) PIC. Moreover, by our choice of \( \varepsilon ,{D}_{a, b}\left( S\right)  - \varepsilon \operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{2} \) id \( \oslash \) id lies in the interior of the PIC cone. Putting these facts together, the assertion follows.

LEMMA 3.9. Suppose that \( S \in  \mathcal{E}\left( b\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) and \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} + \; \frac{2\gamma }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right)  = 0 \) for some pair of orthonormal vectors \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2}}\right\} \) . Then

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} + \frac{2\gamma }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }\right)  > 0.
\]

Proof. We may assume \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2}}\right\} \) are eigenvectors of \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \) , and \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} \; \geq  \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} \) . Let us extend \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2}}\right\} \) to an eigenbasis \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) of \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \) . Clearly, \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{pp} \geq  \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} \) for \( 3 \leq  p \leq  n \) . We compute

\[
\frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} + \frac{2\gamma }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 1}}^{n}\left( {{S}_{1p1p} + {S}_{2p2p}}\right) \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{pp} + \frac{4\left( {1 + \gamma }\right) }{{n}^{2}}\left( {a - b}\right) \operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \frac{2\gamma }{n}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) {\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right| }^{2} - {2b}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}^{2} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2\left( {1 + \gamma }\right) \frac{{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right| }^{2}
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{S}_{1p1p} + {S}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{pp} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{4\left( {1 + \gamma }\right) }{{n}^{2}}\left( {a - b}\right) \operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{2} + \frac{{2\gamma }\left( {1 + \gamma }\right) }{{n}^{2}}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) \operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
- b{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}\right) }^{2} + \frac{2\gamma }{n}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) {\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\left( S\right) \right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ 2\left( {1 + \gamma }\right) \frac{{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }{\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\left( S\right) \right| }^{2}.
\]

Using the identity

\[
2\left( {a - b}\right)  + \gamma \left( {1 - {2b}}\right)  = \frac{b{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}
\]

and the inequality

\[
{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{2{b}^{2}}{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\left( {\left( {{2n} - 1}\right)  + \left( {{3n} - 2}\right) \left( {n - 2}\right) b + \left( {n - 1}\right) {\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}{b}^{2}}\right)  \geq  0,
\]

we obtain

\[
\frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} + \frac{2\gamma }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{S}_{1p1p} + {S}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{pp} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{2\left( {1 + \gamma }\right) }{{n}^{2}}\frac{b{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{2} - b{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}\right) }^{2}.
\]

By Lemma A.3, each eigenvalue of \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \) is bounded from above by the sum of all the other eigenvalues. Therefore,

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p \in  \{ 1,\ldots , n\} \smallsetminus \{ m\} }}\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{pp} \geq  \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{mm}.
\]

Since \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} \leq  0 \) , we deduce that

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p \in  \{ 3,\ldots , n\} \smallsetminus \{ m\} }}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{pp} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{mm} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right)
\]

for each \( m \in  \{ 3,\ldots , n\} \) . Since \( S - T \in \) PIC, it follows that

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{S}_{1p1p} + {S}_{2p2p} - {T}_{1p1p} - {T}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{pp} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right) }\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Since \( T \geq  0 \) , we know that \( {T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p} \geq  0 \) for \( 3 \leq  p \leq  n \) . This gives

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{S}_{1p1p} + {S}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{pp} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{pp} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{1}{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}}\right) .
\]

Putting these facts together, we obtain

\[
\frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} + \frac{2\gamma }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{1}{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{2\left( {1 + \gamma }\right) }{{n}^{2}}\frac{b{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{2} - b{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}\right) }^{2}.
\]

At this point, we distinguish two cases:

Case 1: Suppose that \( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}}\right)  \geq  {2b}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}}\right) \) . In this case, we clearly have

\[
\frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} + \frac{2\gamma }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }\right)  > 0.
\]

Case 2: Suppose next that \( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}}\right)  < {2b}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}}\right) \) . In this case, condition (iv) gives

\[
\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}
\]

\[
\leq  {\omega }^{\frac{1}{2}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}}{\left( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}\right) \right) }^{\frac{1}{2}} + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) b\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}}\right)
\]

\[
< {\omega }^{\frac{1}{2}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}}{\left( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}\right) \right) }^{\frac{1}{2}} + 4\left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}}\right) .
\]

Consequently,

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}}\right)  > \frac{{\left( 1 - 4\left( n - 2\right) {b}^{2}\right) }^{2}}{\omega }\frac{{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}\right) }^{2}}{\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }.
\]

Using the elementary inequality \( {2x} + y \geq  3{\left( {x}^{2}y\right) }^{\frac{1}{3}} \) for \( x, y \geq  0 \) , we obtain

\[
\frac{{\left( 1 - 4\left( n - 2\right) {b}^{2}\right) }^{2}}{2\omega }\frac{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}\right) }{\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }
\]

\[
+ \frac{2\left( {1 + \gamma }\right) }{{n}^{2}}\frac{b{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\frac{\operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{2}}{{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}\right) }^{2}}
\]

\[
\geq  3{\left( \frac{{\left( 1 - 4\left( n - 2\right) {b}^{2}\right) }^{4}}{8{\omega }^{2}}\frac{1 + \gamma }{{n}^{2}}\frac{b{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right) }^{\frac{1}{3}}
\]

\[
= b
\]

where in the last step we have used the definitions of \( \gamma \) and \( \omega \) . Thus, we conclude that

\[
\frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} + \frac{2\gamma }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }\right)
\]

\[
> \frac{{\left( 1 - 4\left( n - 2\right) {b}^{2}\right) }^{2}}{2\omega }\frac{{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}\right) }^{3}}{\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }
\]

\[
+ \frac{2\left( {1 + \gamma }\right) }{{n}^{2}}\frac{b{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{2} - b{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
\geq  0\text{ . }
\]

This proves the assertion.

Lemma 3.10. Suppose that \( S \in  \mathcal{E}\left( b\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} , T \geq  0 \) , and \( S - T \in \) PIC. Moreover, suppose that

\[
\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}
\]

\[
= {\omega }^{\frac{1}{2}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}}{\left( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}\right) \right) }^{\frac{1}{2}} + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) b\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}}\right) .
\]

Then

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}}\right)
\]

\[
< \frac{d}{dt}\left\lbrack  {{\omega }^{\frac{1}{2}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}}{\left( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}\right) \right) }^{\frac{1}{2}} + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) b\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}}\right) }\right\rbrack  .
\]

Proof. If \( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}}\right)  = 0 \) , then the right-hand side is infinite, and the inequality is trivially true. In the following, we assume that \( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{T}_{1p1p} + }\right. \; \left. {T}_{2p2p}\right)  > 0 \) . Clearly, \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} \geq  0 \) and \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{12} = 0 \) . Without loss of generality, we may assume that \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{pq} = 0 \) for \( 3 \leq  p < q \leq  n \) . We may write

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}}\right)  = {J}_{1} + {J}_{2} + {J}_{3} + {J}_{4} + {J}_{5} + {J}_{6},
\]

where

\[
{J}_{1} \mathrel{\text{ := }} 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{S}_{2p2p} - {S}_{1p1p}}\right) \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{pp}
\]

\[
{J}_{2} \mathrel{\text{ := }}  - 4\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}{S}_{121p}\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{2p}
\]

\[
{J}_{3} \mathrel{\text{ := }} 4\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}{S}_{212p}\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{1p}
\]

\[
{J}_{4} \mathrel{\text{ := }}  - 2{S}_{1212}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}}\right) ,
\]

\[
{J}_{5} \mathrel{\text{ := }} {4b}\left( {{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }^{2}\right) }_{11} - {\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }^{2}\right) }_{22}}\right) ,
\]

\[
{J}_{6} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \frac{4}{n}\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}}\right) .
\]

The terms \( {J}_{1},{J}_{2},{J}_{3} \) can be estimated by

\[
{J}_{1} \leq  \tau \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}{\left( {S}_{2p2p} - {S}_{1p1p}\right) }^{2} + \frac{1}{\tau }\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{pp}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
{J}_{2} \leq  \frac{2\left( {n - 2}\right) \tau }{n - 3}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}{\left( {S}_{121p}\right) }^{2} + \frac{2\left( {n - 3}\right) }{\left( {n - 2}\right) \tau }\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{2p}\right) }^{2},
\]

\[
{J}_{3} \leq  \frac{2\left( {n - 2}\right) \tau }{n - 3}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}{\left( {S}_{212p}\right) }^{2} + \frac{2\left( {n - 3}\right) }{\left( {n - 2}\right) \tau }\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{1p}\right) }^{2},
\]

where \( \tau \) is an arbitrary positive number. To estimate \( {J}_{4} \) , we observe that

\[
0 \leq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{3 \leq  p, q \leq  n, p \neq  q}}\left( {{S}_{1212} + {S}_{1p1p} + {S}_{2q2q} + {S}_{pqpq}}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {n - 3}\right) {S}_{1212} + \left( {n - 4}\right) \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{S}_{1p1p} + {S}_{2p2p}}\right)  + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{pp}
\]

since \( S \in \) PIC. This gives

\[
{J}_{4} \leq  \frac{2\left( {n - 4}\right) }{\left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {n - 3}\right) }\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{S}_{1p1p} + {S}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{2}{\left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {n - 3}\right) }\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}}\right) \left( {\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{pp}}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{2\left( {n - 4}\right) }{\left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {n - 3}\right) }\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{S}_{1p1p} + {S}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{2}{\left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {n - 3}\right) }\left( {\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{S}_{2p2p} - {S}_{1p1p}}\right) }\right) \left( {\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{pp}}\right) ,
\]

hence

\[
{J}_{4} \leq  \frac{\left( {n - 2}\right) \tau }{n - 3}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}{\left( {S}_{1p1p} + {S}_{2p2p}\right) }^{2} + \frac{{\left( n - 4\right) }^{2}}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}\left( {n - 3}\right) \tau }{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \frac{\tau }{n - 3}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}{\left( {S}_{2p2p} - {S}_{1p1p}\right) }^{2} + \frac{1}{\left( {n - 3}\right) \tau }\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{pp}\right) }^{2}
\]

for each \( \tau  > 0 \) . Adding these inequalities gives

\[
{J}_{1} + {J}_{2} + {J}_{3} + {J}_{4}
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{2\left( {n - 2}\right) \tau }{n - 3}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\left( {S}_{1p1p}\right) }^{2} + {\left( {S}_{2p2p}\right) }^{2} + {\left( {S}_{121p}\right) }^{2} + {\left( {S}_{212p}\right) }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{n - 2}{\left( {n - 3}\right) \tau }\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{pp}\right) }^{2} + \frac{2\left( {n - 3}\right) }{\left( {n - 2}\right) \tau }\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{1p}\right) }^{2} + {\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{2p}\right) }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{{\left( n - 4\right) }^{2}}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}\left( {n - 3}\right) \tau }{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{\left( {n - 2}\right) \tau }{n - 3}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\left( {S}^{2}\right) }_{1p1p} + {\left( {S}^{2}\right) }_{2p2p}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{n - 2}{\left( {n - 3}\right) \tau }{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right| }^{2} - \frac{n - 2}{2\left( {n - 3}\right) \tau }{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}\right) }^{2}
\]

for each \( \tau  > 0 \) . Moreover,

\[
{J}_{5} \leq   - {4b}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right)  + {4b}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{1p}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
=  - {4b}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{S}_{2p2p} - {S}_{1p1p}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {4b}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}{\left( {S}_{12p2} + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{q = 3}}^{n}{S}_{1qpq}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  8\left( {n - 3}\right) {b}^{2}\tau \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}{\left( {S}_{2p2p} - {S}_{1p1p}\right) }^{2} + \frac{n - 2}{2\left( {n - 3}\right) \tau }{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ 4\left( {n - 2}\right) b\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\left( {S}_{12p2}\right) }^{2} + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{q = 3}}^{n}{\left( {S}_{1qpq}\right) }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {8\left( {n - 3}\right) {b}^{2}\tau  + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\left( {S}^{2}\right) }_{1p1p} + {\left( {S}^{2}\right) }_{2p2p}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{n - 2}{2\left( {n - 3}\right) \tau }{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}\right) }^{2}
\]

for each \( \tau  > 0 \) . Finally,

\[
{J}_{6} = \frac{4}{n}\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) \left( {\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{S}_{2p2p} - {S}_{1p1p}}\right) }\right) \left( {\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 1}}^{n}\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{pp}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{2\left( {n - 2}\right) \tau }{n}\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}{\left( {S}_{2p2p} - {S}_{1p1p}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \frac{2\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) }{\tau }{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{2\left( {n - 2}\right) \tau }{n}\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\left( {S}^{2}\right) }_{1p1p} + {\left( {S}^{2}\right) }_{2p2p}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{2\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) }{\tau }{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right| }^{2}
\]

for each \( \tau  > 0 \) . Putting these facts together, we obtain

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \left\lbrack  {\left( {\frac{n - 2}{n - 3} + \frac{2\left( {n - 2}\right) }{n}\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right)  + 8\left( {n - 3}\right) {b}^{2}}\right) \tau  + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
\cdot  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\left( {S}^{2}\right) }_{1p1p} + {\left( {S}^{2}\right) }_{2p2p}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \left( {\frac{n - 2}{n - 3} + 2\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) }\right) \frac{1}{\tau }{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right| }^{2}
\]

for each \( \tau  > 0 \) . If we put \( \tau  = {2\sigma }\left( {\frac{n - 2}{n - 3} + 2\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) }\right) \) and use the inequality

\[
\left( {\frac{n - 2}{n - 3} + \frac{2\left( {n - 2}\right) }{n}\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right)  + 8\left( {n - 3}\right) {b}^{2}}\right) \left( {\frac{n - 2}{n - 3} + 2\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) }\right)  \leq  \frac{\omega }{2}
\]

(cf. Lemma 3.3), we conclude that for each \( \sigma  > 0 \) ,

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {{\omega \sigma } + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\left( {S}^{2}\right) }_{1p1p} + {\left( {S}^{2}\right) }_{2p2p}}\right)  + \frac{1}{2\sigma }{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right| }^{2}.
\]

On the other hand, Lemma 3.6 implies \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( S\right) }\right)  > 0 \) , hence \( \frac{d}{dt}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) \; > 2{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right| }^{2} \) . Using the inequality

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}}\right)  > \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\left( {S}^{2}\right) }_{1p1p} + {\left( {S}^{2}\right) }_{2p2p}}\right) ,
\]

we obtain

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left\lbrack  {{\omega }^{\frac{1}{2}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}}{\left( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}\right) \right) }^{\frac{1}{2}} + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) b\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}}\right) }\right\rbrack
\]

\[
> \left( {{\omega \sigma } + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\left( {S}^{2}\right) }_{1p1p} + {\left( {S}^{2}\right) }_{2p2p}}\right)  + \frac{1}{2\sigma }{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right| }^{2},
\]

where \( \sigma  \mathrel{\text{ := }} \frac{1}{2}{\omega }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}}{\left( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}\right) \right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) . Putting these facts together, the assertion follows.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
a) If one carries out everything in this section in the special case that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a Kähler manifold, then the holonomy group of the connection \( \nabla \) is isomorphic to a subgroup of \( \mathrm{U}\left( {{T}_{p}M}\right)  \rtimes  {T}_{p}M \subset  \mathrm{{SO}}\left( {{T}_{p}M}\right)  \rtimes  {T}_{p}M \) and the image of the Harnack operator is contained in the Lie subalgebra \( {\mathfrak{g}}^{\prime } \) of this group. One can then formulate and prove an analogous statement for Harnack operators of Kähler manifolds.

b) Let \( \mathrm{{Hk}} \) be a Harnack operator and \( R = {\mathrm{{Hk}}}_{\mid {so}\left( n\right) } \) . A simple computation shows that the trace Harnack inequality is equivalent to

\[
\inf \left\{  {\operatorname{tr}\left( {{\mathrm{{Ad}}}_{v}{\mathrm{{HkAd}}}_{v}^{tr}}\right)  \mid  v \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \subset  \operatorname{Iso}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) }\right\}   - \operatorname{tr}\left( R\right)  \geq  0.
\]

If \( R \) has positive Ricci curvature, then there is a unique \( v \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) such that \( {\mathrm{{Ad}}}_{v}\mathrm{{Hk}}{\mathrm{{Ad}}}_{v}^{tr} \) has minimal trace.

c) The reason for the somewhat complicated approach toward the maximum principle is that it is in general not true that a convex set \( C\left( t\right) \) is contained in the interior of another slightly larger convex set \( C \) which is also invariant under the action of \( \operatorname{Iso}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) , cf. next subsection. This is of course related to the fact that the connection is not compatible with a metric on the space of curvature tensors.

knowledge_statements.title: Fine versus Coarse Ricci-Flow Estimates
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fine versus Coarse Ricci-Flow Estimates
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
1.1. The distinction between fine and coarse estimates. It is useful to distinguish between what we may call fine estimates with what we may call coarse estimates. Since we apply these terminologies in a casual way, we describe our distinction between them in terms of examples. Examples of fine estimates in the theory of Ricci flow are curvature pinching estimates, Harnack-type estimates, entropy formulas, and monotonicity formulas. We may decree that an aspect of the fineness of an estimate is its sensitivity to perturbation. \( {}^{1} \) Although the matrix and trace Harnack estimates for the Ricci flow are known assuming nonnegative curvature operator in dimensions 2 and above, so far no substantial improvements (i.e., perturbations) seem to be known for dimensions 3 and above (in dimension 2 there is a trace Harnack estimate for arbitrary solutions on closed surfaces). On the other hand, one may think of the Hamilton-Ivey curvature estimate as a perturbation of the 'nonnegative sectional curvature is preserved' estimate in dimension 3. In this sense Harnack-type estimates appear finer than curvature pinching estimates although an analogy exists between them via the space-time approach. \( {}^{2} \) A further comment is that curvature pinching estimates in dimension 3 may be thought of as (large) perturbations of the 'nonnegative sectional (or Ricci) curvature is preserved' estimate.

Another aspect of the fineness of an estimate is how sharp it is; in general, finer estimates are sharper. A classical sharp example in Riemannian geometry is the Bishop-Gromov volume comparison theorem. In the Ricci flow, the matrix Harnack estimate is sharp (i.e., equality is attained in certain directions) on expanding gradient Ricci solitons. Moreover, for the corresponding Harnack estimate for ancient solutions we have that equality is attained on steady gradient Ricci solitons. Strikingly, Perelman has proved sharp monotonicity formulas for complete solutions of the Ricci flow on both closed and noncompact manifolds (without curvature sign restrictions). These estimates are sharp, as are monotonicity formulas in geometric flows in general.

On the other hand, in deriving coarse estimates, the ability to successfully apply the maximum principle to the evolution equations of the relevant quantities does not depend in a sensitive way on the constants in these quantities. For this reason we consider the global and local derivative of curvature estimates to be coarse estimates. Perhaps for the same reason derivative estimates hold for a number of different geometric evolution equations besides the Ricci flow including the heat equation on Riemannian manifolds and the mean curvature flow.

---

\( {}^{1} \) That is, the finer the estimate, the more difficult it is to perturb.

\( {}^{2} \) However, the reader may argue that a Harnack estimate in dimension \( n \) corresponds to a curvature estimate in dimension \( n + 1 \) since time adds a dimension, so that the apparent increase in fineness really corresponds to an increase in dimension.

---

The fineness or coarseness of an estimate may not be related to its relative importance to the study of a geometric flow; however, it may be related to its geometric significance. We venture to say that, in general, finer estimates are positively correlated to more geometrically significant estimates. An example of what we mean by this is that in many monotonicity formulas, the equality case, i.e., the case where the geometric invariant is constant under the flow, is characterized as occurring if and only if the solution is self-similar.

It is straightforward to check that \( X \mathrel{\text{ := }} \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{{\operatorname{Ad}}_{tv}{\operatorname{HkAd}}_{vt}^{tr}}{{t}^{2}} \) is a traceless operator in \( W \) . Clearly \( X \in  {\partial }_{\infty }C \) .

Since the traceless operators \( {W}^{\prime } \subset  W \) form an irreducible subspace we deduce that \( {W}^{\prime } \subset  {\partial }_{\infty }C \) . Let \( C\left( t\right) \) be as in the lemma.

Consider the element \( - \mathrm{{id}} \in  O\left( n\right) \) and let \( \operatorname{Fix}\left( {-\mathrm{{id}}}\right)  \subset  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( \mathfrak{g}\right) \) denote the fixed point set of - id. Notice that \( \operatorname{Fix}\left( {-\mathrm{{id}}}\right) \) is still invariant under \( \operatorname{SO}\left( n\right) \) . It is easy to see that \( \operatorname{Fix}\left( {-{id}}\right)  \cap  C \) has maximal dimension in \( \operatorname{Fix}\left( {-\mathrm{{id}}}\right) \) . Moreover the set \( \widetilde{C}\left( t\right)  = C\left( t\right)  \cap  \operatorname{Fix}\left( {-\mathrm{{id}}}\right) \) is invariant under the ODE.

Notice that \( \widetilde{C}\left( 0\right) \) contains a subset of the form \( {\lambda I} + {W}^{\prime } \) where \( I \) is the orthogonal projection of \( \mathfrak{g} \) to \( \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) \) for some \( \lambda \) . If we evolve this set under the ODE we see that \( {W}^{\prime } \subset  {\partial }_{\infty }C\left( t\right) \) for all \( t \) .

Thus \( \widetilde{C}\left( t\right)  = \widetilde{C}{\left( t\right) }^{\prime } + {W}^{\prime } \) where \( \widetilde{C}{\left( t\right) }^{\prime } \subset  {W}^{\prime  \bot  } \cap  \operatorname{Fix}\left( {-\mathrm{{id}}}\right) \) is convex.

We may assume that the norm of \( {\mathrm{{Hk}}}_{\mid \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right)  \times  \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) } \) is bounded by some a priori constant for all \( \mathrm{{Hk}} \in  C\left( t\right) \) . This in turn implies that a sequence in \( \widetilde{C}{\left( t\right) }^{\prime } \) tends to \( \infty \) if and only if its trace is unbounded.

Using that \( \widetilde{C}\left( t\right) \) is invariant under the ODE and that \( {C}^{\prime }\left( t\right) \) has full dimension it is easy to see that for all positive \( t \) there are endomorphisms with arbitrary small as well as endomorphisms with arbitrary large trace in \( \widetilde{C}\left( t\right) \) and hence in \( \widetilde{C}{\left( t\right) }^{\prime } \) . Therefore \( W \subset  {\partial }_{\infty }\widetilde{C}\left( t\right) \) . This implies as before \( V \subset  {\partial }_{\infty }C\left( t\right) \) for all positive \( t \) as claimed.

The complexification of \( \mathrm{U}\left( n\right)  \rtimes  {\mathbb{C}}^{n} \) is given by \( \operatorname{GL}\left( {n,\mathbb{C}}\right)  \rtimes \; \left( {{\mathbb{C}}^{n} \oplus  {\mathbb{C}}^{n}}\right) \) , where \( \mathrm{{GL}}\left( {n,\mathbb{C}}\right) \) acts in the standard way on the first summand and by \( \left( {A, v}\right)  \mapsto  {\left( {\bar{A}}^{tr}\right) }^{-1}v \) on the second \( {\mathbb{C}}^{n} \) -summand. Thus the set

\[
S \mathrel{\text{ := }} \left\{  {\left( {A, v,0}\right)  \in  \mathfrak{{gl}}\left( {n,\mathbb{C}}\right)  \times  {\mathbb{C}}^{n} \times  {\mathbb{C}}^{n} \mid  \operatorname{rank}\left( A\right)  = 1, v \in  A\left( {\mathbb{C}}^{n}\right) }\right\}  ,
\]

is invariant under the coadjoint representation. This gives a Harnack inequality for Kähler manifolds with positive bisectional curvature whose trace form is similar to Cao's [1992] Harnack inequality.

b) Let \( \left( {\mathfrak{g},\langle \cdot , \cdot  \rangle }\right) \) be as in the proposition and let \( G : \mathfrak{g} \rightarrow  \mathfrak{g} \) denote a selfadjoint positive endomorphism. Put \( g\left( {v, w}\right)  = \langle  \cdot  , G \cdot  \rangle \) . The ODE \( {R}^{\prime } = {R}^{{\# }_{g}} \) corresponding to the metric Lie algebra \( \left( {\mathfrak{g}, g}\right) \) is obtained by pulling back the corresponding ODE for the metric Lie algebra \( \left( {\mathfrak{g},\langle \cdot , \cdot  \rangle }\right) \) under the linear map \( {S}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{g}, g}\right)  \rightarrow  {S}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{g},\langle \cdot , \cdot  \rangle }\right) , R \mapsto  R{G}^{-1} \) . Suppose, on the contrary, we can find \( {\mathrm{{Hk}}}_{i} \in  C \) and \( {v}_{i} \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) such that the Ricci curvature \( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{i} \) of \( {\operatorname{Hk}}_{i \mid  \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right)  \times  \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) } \) satisfies the following \( \left( {i = 1,2}\right)  : {\operatorname{Ric}}_{1}\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{1}}\right)  > \) 0 and \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{2}}\right)  < 0 \) . Put \( {\mathrm{{Hk}}}_{i}\left( t\right)  = {\mathrm{{Ad}}}_{t{v}_{i}}{\mathrm{{Hk}}}_{i}{\mathrm{{Ad}}}_{t{v}_{i}}^{tr} \) . It is straightforward to check that the trace \( \operatorname{tr}\left( {{\mathrm{{Hk}}}_{i}\left( t\right) }\right) \) converges quadratically in \( t \) to \( {\left( -1\right) }^{i + 1}\infty \) as \( t \rightarrow  \infty \; \left( {i = 1,2}\right) \) . The element \( {X}_{i} = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{{\mathrm{{Hk}}}_{i}\left( t\right) }{{t}^{2}} \) is an element in the cone at infinity

\[
{\partial }_{\infty }C \mathrel{\text{ := }} \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\lambda  \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{C}{\lambda }
\]

of \( C \) . We know \( \operatorname{tr}\left( {X}_{1}\right)  > 0,\operatorname{tr}\left( {X}_{2}\right)  < 0 \) and it is straightforward to check \( {X}_{i} \in  W \) . Moreover the operator \( {X}_{i} \) has \( {v}_{i} \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) in its kernel.

Clearly the cone \( {\partial }_{\infty }C \) is invariant under the the representation of \( \operatorname{Iso}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) . The barry center of the \( \mathrm{{SO}}\left( n\right) \) -orbit of \( {X}_{1} \) (resp. \( {X}_{2} \) ) is a positive (resp. negative) multiple of the orthogonal projection of \( \mathfrak{g} \) to \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) .

Under \( \mathrm{{SO}}\left( n\right) \) the vectorspace \( W \) decomposes into a one dimensional trivial and an irreducible representation. Since \( {X}_{i} \in  W \) itself is not a multiple of the orthogonal projection we can also find a traceless operator \( X \in  {\partial }_{\infty }C \cap  W \) . Clearly this implies \( W \subset  {\partial }_{\infty }C \) .

The quotient space \( V/W \) decomposes under \( \mathrm{{SO}}\left( n\right) \) in two inequivalent irreducible nontrivial subrepresentations.

Using that \( C \) has maximal dimension we can find \( \mathrm{{Hk}} \in  C \) such that for some \( v \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n},\left( {{\operatorname{Ad}}_{v}{\mathrm{{HkAd}}}_{v}^{tr} - \mathrm{{Hk}}}\right)  \in  V \) projects to an element in \( V/W \) which is not contained in a nontrivial invariant subspace.

For each \( t \) we choose \( Y\left( t\right)  \in  W \) such that \( L\left( t\right)  \mathrel{\text{ := }} {\operatorname{Ad}}_{t}v\operatorname{Hk}{\operatorname{Ad}}_{t}{v}^{tr} - Y\left( t\right) \) has minimal norm. It then follows that the norm of \( L \) increases linearly and \( {L}_{\infty } \mathrel{\text{ := }} \; \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{L\left( t\right) }{t} \in  V \cap  {\partial }_{\infty }C \) corresponds in \( V/W \) to an element that does not lie in a nontrivial invariant subspace.

This in turn shows \( V \subset  {\partial }_{\infty }C \) and hence \( C \) is of the form \( {C}^{\prime } + V \) .

knowledge_statements.title: Ancient Blow-Up Limits at Finite-Time Singularities
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ancient Blow-Up Limits at Finite-Time Singularities
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose we have a solution to the Ricci Flow on a compact manifold \( {M}^{m} \) of dimension \( m \) with weakly positive curvature operator for a maximal time interval \( 0 \leq  t < T \) . Then we can find a sequence of dilations which converge to a complete solution of the Ricci Flow with curvature bounded at each time on an ancient time interval \( - \infty  < t < \Omega \) with scalar curvature \( R \) bounded by

\[
R \leq  \Omega /\left( {\Omega  - t}\right)
\]

everywhere and \( R = 1 \) at some origin \( O \) at time \( t = 0 \) , which again has weakly positive curvature operator. Moreover the limit splits as a quotient of a product \( {N}^{n} \times  {R}^{k} \) with \( m = n + k \) flat in the directions \( {R}^{k} \) with \( k \geq  0 \) , and where the interesting factor \( {N}^{n} \) either is compact or has finite asymptotic curvature ratio

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{s \rightarrow  \infty }}R{s}^{2} = A < \infty
\]

Moreover the limit factor \( {N}^{n} \) will still satisfy a local injectivity radius estimate.

Of course we conjecture the only possible limit is the round sphere \( {S}^{n} \) or a quotient of it shrinking to a point. In dimension 3 or 4 we have pinching estimates that keep the curvature operator strictly positive if it starts strictly positive, that prevent limits \( {N}^{n} \times  {R}^{k} \) with \( k > 0 \) . We do not know any examples of complete non compact ancient solutions of positive curvature operator with \( R{s}^{2} < \infty \) and \( R\left| t\right|  < \infty \) , and we conjecture none exist, since the curvature has had plenty of space and time to dissipate.

knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
Suppose \( n \geq  4 \) . Notice that the cone \( C \) of 2-nonnegative curvature operators satisfies the assumptions of Proposition 3.2. We plan to show that the family of closed invariant cones from Proposition 3.2 can be extended to a pinching family. By the above remark it suffices to show that \( {\mathrm{l}}_{a\left( b\right) , b}\left( C\right) \) is contained in the cone of nonnegative curvature operators where \( b \) is the maximal allowed value from Proposition 3.2. In fact then we can extend the family from Proposition 3.2 to a pinching family by defining it on the second part of the interval as a reparametrization of the pinching family \( {\left( C\left( s\right)  \cap  {C}^{\prime }\right) }_{s \in  \lbrack 0,1)} \) where \( {C}^{\prime } \mathrel{\text{ := }} {\mathrm{l}}_{a\left( b\right) , b}\left( C\right) \) .

Let \( \mathrm{R} \in  C \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) . Recall that by (7) we have \( {\mathrm{l}}_{a, b}\left( \mathrm{R}\right)  = \mathrm{R} + {2b}\operatorname{Ric} \land  \mathrm{{id}} + h{\mathrm{R}}_{I} \) for \( h \mathrel{\text{ := }} 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \) . The smallest eigenvalue of \( \mathrm{R} \) is by a standard estimate larger than or equal to \( - \frac{2\operatorname{tr}\left( \mathrm{R}\right) }{n\left( {n - 1}\right)  - 4} \) . Moreover, since the sum of the two smallest eigenvalues of \( \mathrm{R} \) is nonnegative the smallest eigenvalue of Ric is bounded from below by \( \left( {n - 3}\right) \) times the absolute value of the smallest eigenvalue of \( \mathrm{R} \) . Thus in order to show that \( {\mathrm{l}}_{a, b}\left( \mathrm{R}\right)  \geq  0 \) it is sufficient to prove \( h \geq  \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) \frac{n\left( {n - 1}\right) }{n\left( {n - 1}\right)  - 4} \) . This is equivalent to

\[
\left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} \geq  \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) \frac{n}{n\left( {n - 1}\right)  - 4}.
\]

By the definition of \( b \) we have \( \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} = \frac{2}{n}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) \) . This shows the claim for \( n \geq  4 \) . For \( n = 3 \) , Theorem 3.1 is well known.

knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
By equation (3)

\[
\mathrm{R} = {\mathrm{R}}_{I} + {\mathrm{R}}_{{\mathrm{{Ric}}}_{0}} = \frac{\bar{\lambda }}{\left( n - 1\right) }I + \frac{2}{\left( n - 2\right) }{\operatorname{Ric}}_{0} \land  \mathrm{{id}}.
\]

Using the abbreviation \( {\mathrm{R}}_{0} = {\mathrm{R}}_{{\mathrm{{Ric}}}_{0}} \) we have

\[
{\mathrm{R}}^{2} + {\mathrm{R}}^{\# } = {\mathrm{R}}_{0}^{2} + {\mathrm{R}}_{0}^{\# } + \frac{2\bar{\lambda }}{\left( n - 1\right) }\left( {{\mathrm{R}}_{0} + {\mathrm{R}}_{0}\# I}\right)  + \frac{{\bar{\lambda }}^{2}}{{\left( n - 1\right) }^{2}}\left( {I + {I}^{\# }}\right) .
\]

Since the last two summands are known by Lemma 2.1, we may assume that \( \mathrm{R} = {\mathrm{R}}_{{\mathrm{{Ric}}}_{0}} \) . Let \( {\lambda }_{1},\ldots ,{\lambda }_{n} \) denote the eigenvalues of \( {\mathrm{{Ric}}}_{0} \) corresponding to an orthonormal basis \( {e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n} \) of \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . The curvature operator \( \mathrm{R} \) is diagonal with respect to \( {e}_{1} \land  {e}_{2},\ldots ,{e}_{n - 1} \land  {e}_{n} \) and we denote by \( {\mathrm{R}}_{ij} = \frac{{\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{j}}{n - 2} \) the corresponding eigenvalues for \( 1 \leq  i < j \leq  n \) . Inspection of (4) shows that also \( {\mathrm{R}}^{2} + {\mathrm{R}}^{\# } \) is diagonal with respect to this basis. We have

\[
{\left( {\mathrm{R}}^{2} + {\mathrm{R}}^{\# }\right) }_{ij} = {\mathrm{R}}_{ij}^{2} + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k \neq  i, j}}{\mathrm{R}}_{ik}{\mathrm{R}}_{jk}
\]

\[
= \frac{{\left( {\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{j}\right) }^{2}}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}} + \frac{1}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k \neq  i, j}}\left( {{\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{k}}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{j} + {\lambda }_{k}}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{{\lambda }_{i}{\lambda }_{j}}{\left( n - 2\right) } + \frac{{n\sigma } - {\lambda }_{i}^{2} - {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}
\]

as claimed.

The second identity follows immediately from the first. To show the last identity notice that the Ricci tensor of \( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0} \land  {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0} \) is given by \( - {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}^{2} \) . A computation shows the claim.

knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
The proof is essentially the same as in Section 11.7 in Perelman's paper [33] (see also [12]). We sketch the argument for the convenience of the reader. Let us fix a point \( y \in  M \) . By rescaling, we can arrange that \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right)  = 1 \) . For abbreviation, let \( A = \left\{  {x \in  M : \operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right) {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, x\right) }^{2} \geq  1}\right\} \) . We distinguish two cases:

Case 1: Suppose that \( A = \varnothing \) . In this case, we can find a point \( z \in  M \) such that \( \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  = \operatorname{scal}\left( {z,0}\right) \) . Using the Harnack inequality, we obtain

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {z,0}\right)
\]

for all \( t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) . By Shi’s derivative estimates, \( \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\operatorname{scal}\left( {z, t}\right)  \leq  C\left( n\right) \operatorname{scal}{\left( z,0\right) }^{2} \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-\operatorname{scal}{\left( z,0\right) }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) . Moreover, \( {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right)  \leq  \operatorname{scal}{\left( z,0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) since \( A = \varnothing \) . Hence, we can find a small positive constant \( \beta \) , depending only on \( n \) , such that for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-\beta \operatorname{scal}{\left( z,0\right) }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) ,

\[
\operatorname{scal}\left( {z, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{scal}\left( {z,0}\right) \;\text{ and }\;{d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {y, z}\right)  \leq  2\operatorname{scal}{\left( z,0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}.
\]

If we apply the Harnack inequality (cf. Corollary 6.3) with \( t =  - \beta \operatorname{scal}{\left( z,0\right) }^{-1} \) , then we obtain

\[
\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{scal}\left( {z,0}\right)  \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {z, t}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \exp \left( \frac{{d}_{g\left( t\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{2}}{\left( -2t\right) }\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \exp \left( \frac{2}{\left( {-t}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( {z,0}\right) }\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right)
\]

\[
= \exp \left( \frac{2}{\beta }\right) \text{ . }
\]

Putting these facts together, we conclude that \( \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  2\exp \left( \frac{2}{\beta }\right) \) .

Case 2: Suppose now that \( A \neq  \varnothing \) . In this case, we choose a point \( z \in  A \) that has minimal distance from \( y \) with respect to the metric \( g\left( 0\right) \) . Note that \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {z,0}\right)  = {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-2} \) since \( z \) lies on the boundary of \( A \) . Let \( p \) be the mid-point of the minimizing geodesic in \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) joining \( y \) and \( z \) . Clearly, \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p,\frac{1}{4}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) }\right)  \cap  A = \varnothing \) . This implies

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p,\frac{1}{4}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) }\right) }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  {16}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-2}.
\]

By the Harnack inequality,

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {p,\frac{1}{4}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) }\right) }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {16}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-2}
\]

for all \( t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) . The noncollapsing assumption gives

\[
{\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {{B}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {p,\frac{1}{4}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) }\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {\left( \frac{1}{4}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( y, z\right) \right) }^{n}
\]

for all \( t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) . This implies

\[
{\left( 4r\right) }^{-n}{\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {{B}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {p,{4r}}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {\left( \frac{1}{16}{r}^{-1}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( y, z\right) \right) }^{n}
\]

for all \( t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) and all \( r \geq  {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) \) . Applying Theorem 6.12 with \( {x}_{0} \mathrel{\text{ := }} p \) , \( {r}_{0} \mathrel{\text{ := }} {4r} \) , and \( w \mathrel{\text{ := }} \kappa {\left( \frac{1}{16}{r}^{-1}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( y, z\right) \right) }^{n} \) , we obtain

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r}\right) }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-2}\omega \left( {{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-1}r}\right)
\]

for all \( r \geq  {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) \) , where \( \omega  : \lbrack 1,\infty ) \rightarrow  \lbrack 0,\infty ) \) is a positive and increasing function that may depend on \( n \) and \( \kappa \) . In particular, if we put \( r = {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) \) and apply the Harnack inequality, we obtain

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p,{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) }\right) }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-2}\omega \left( 1\right) ,
\]

for all \( t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) . By Shi’s derivative estimates,

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\operatorname{scal}\left( {z, t}\right)  \leq  C\left( {n,\kappa }\right) {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-4}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{2},0}\right\rbrack \) . Moreover, \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {z,0}\right)  = {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-2} \) by our choice of \( z \) . Therefore, we can find a small positive constant \( \beta \) , depending only on \( n \) and \( \kappa \) , such that \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {z, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{2}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-2} \) and \( {d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {y, z}\right)  \leq  2{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-\beta {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{2},0}\right\rbrack \) . If we apply the Harnack inequality (cf. Corollary 6.3) with \( t =  - \beta {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{2} \) , then we obtain

\[
\frac{1}{2}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-2} \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {z, t}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \exp \left( \frac{{d}_{g\left( t\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{2}}{\left( -2t\right) }\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \exp \left( \frac{2{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{2}}{\left( -t\right) }\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right)
\]

\[
= \exp \left( \frac{2}{\beta }\right) \text{ . }
\]

This finally implies

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, r}\right) }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r + {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) }\right) }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-2}\omega \left( {{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-1}r + 1}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  2{e}^{\frac{2}{\beta }}\omega \left( {\sqrt{2}{e}^{\frac{1}{\beta }}r + 1}\right)
\]

for all \( r \geq  0 \) . This completes the proof of Theorem 6.13.

a) Using Remark 2.4 and the proposition in the case that \( \mathfrak{g} \) is given by the Lie algebra of \( \mathrm{U}\left( n\right)  \rtimes  {\mathbb{C}}^{n} \) one can derive Harnack inequalities for Kähler manifolds. The complexification of \( \mathrm{U}\left( n\right)  \rtimes  {\mathbb{C}}^{n} \) is given by \( \operatorname{GL}\left( {n,\mathbb{C}}\right)  \rtimes \; \left( {{\mathbb{C}}^{n} \oplus  {\mathbb{C}}^{n}}\right) \) , where \( \mathrm{{GL}}\left( {n,\mathbb{C}}\right) \) acts in the standard way on the first summand and by \( \left( {A, v}\right)  \mapsto  {\left( {\bar{A}}^{tr}\right) }^{-1}v \) on the second \( {\mathbb{C}}^{n} \) -summand. Thus the set

\[
S \mathrel{\text{ := }} \left\{  {\left( {A, v,0}\right)  \in  \mathfrak{{gl}}\left( {n,\mathbb{C}}\right)  \times  {\mathbb{C}}^{n} \times  {\mathbb{C}}^{n} \mid  \operatorname{rank}\left( A\right)  = 1, v \in  A\left( {\mathbb{C}}^{n}\right) }\right\}  ,
\]

is invariant under the coadjoint representation. This gives a Harnack inequality for Kähler manifolds with positive bisectional curvature whose trace form is similar to Cao's [1992] Harnack inequality.

b) Let \( \left( {\mathfrak{g},\langle \cdot , \cdot  \rangle }\right) \) be as in the proposition and let \( G : \mathfrak{g} \rightarrow  \mathfrak{g} \) denote a selfadjoint positive endomorphism. Put \( g\left( {v, w}\right)  = \langle  \cdot  , G \cdot  \rangle \) . The ODE \( {R}^{\prime } = {R}^{{\# }_{g}} \) corresponding to the metric Lie algebra \( \left( {\mathfrak{g}, g}\right) \) is obtained by pulling back the corresponding ODE for the metric Lie algebra \( \left( {\mathfrak{g},\langle \cdot , \cdot  \rangle }\right) \) under the linear map \( {S}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{g}, g}\right)  \rightarrow  {S}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{g},\langle \cdot , \cdot  \rangle }\right) , R \mapsto  R{G}^{-1} \) . Thus \( {R}^{{\# }_{g}} = {\left( R{G}^{-1}\right) }^{\# } \cdot  G \) .
