Let \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) , x \in  M \) and \( t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) , be a nonflat ancient \( \kappa \) -solution for some \( \kappa  > 0 \) . For an arbitrary point \( \left( {p,{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  M \times  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) , we define as in Chapter 3 that

\[
\tau  = {t}_{0} - t,\;\text{ for }t < {t}_{0},
\]

\[
l\left( {q,\tau }\right)  = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\tau }}\inf \left\{  {{\int }_{0}^{\tau }\sqrt{s}\left( {R\left( {\gamma \left( s\right) ,{t}_{0} - s}\right)  + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( s\right) \right| }_{{g}_{ij}\left( {{t}_{0} - s}\right) }^{2}}\right) {ds} \mid  }\right.
\]

\[
\gamma  : \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M\text{ with }\left. {\gamma \left( 0\right)  = p,\gamma \left( \tau \right)  = q}\right\}  ,
\]

\[
\text{ and }\widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right)  = {\int }_{M}{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,\tau }\right) }\right) d{V}_{{t}_{0} - \tau }\left( q\right) \text{ . }
\]

Recall from (6.2.1) that for each \( \tau  > 0 \) we can find \( q = q\left( \tau \right) \) such that \( l\left( {q,\tau }\right)  \leq  \frac{3}{2} \) . In view of Lemma 6.4.1, we may assume that the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution is not a gradient shrinking Ricci soliton. Thus by (the proof of) Theorem 6.2.1, the scalings of \( {g}_{ij}\left( {{t}_{0} - \tau }\right) \) at \( q\left( \tau \right) \) with factor \( {\tau }^{-1} \) converge along a subsequence of \( \tau  \rightarrow   + \infty \) to a nonflat gradient shrinking soliton with nonnegative curvature operator which is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales. We now show that the limit has bounded curvature.

Denote the limiting nonflat gradient shrinking soliton by \( \left( {\bar{M},{\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) with \( - \infty  < \; t \leq  0 \) . Note that there holds the Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality (Theorem 2.5.4) on any ancient \( \kappa \) -solution and in particular, the scalar curvature of the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution is pointwise nondecreasing in time. This implies that the scalar curvature of the limiting soliton \( \left( {\bar{M},{\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) is still pointwise nondecreasing in time. Thus we only need to show that the limiting soliton has bounded curvature at \( t = 0 \) .

We argue by contradiction. By lifting to its orientable cover, we may assume that \( \bar{M} \) is orientable. Suppose the curvature of the limiting soliton is unbounded at \( t = 0 \) . Of course in this case the limiting soliton \( \bar{M} \) is noncompact. Then by applying Lemma 6.1.4, we can choose a sequence of points \( {x}_{j}, j = 1,2,\ldots \) , divergent to infinity such that the scalar curvature \( \bar{R} \) of the limit satisfies

\[
\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right)  \geq  j\text{ and }\bar{R}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  4\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  {B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{j}, j/\sqrt{\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) }}\right) \) and \( j = 1,2,\ldots \) Since the scalar curvature is nondecreasing in time, we have

(6.4.10)

\[
\bar{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  4\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) ,
\]

for all \( x \in  {B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{j}, j/\sqrt{\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) }}\right) \) , all \( t \leq  0 \) and \( j = 1,2,\ldots \) By combining with Hamilton’s compactness theorem (Theorem 4.1.5) and the \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing, we know that a subsequence of the rescaled solutions

\[
\left( {\bar{M},\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) {\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( {x, t/\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) }\right) ,{x}_{j}}\right) ,\;j = 1,2,\ldots ,
\]

converges in the \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) topology to a nonflat smooth solution of the Ricci flow. Then Proposition 6.1.2 implies that the new limit at the new time \( \{ t = 0\} \) must split off a line. By pulling back the new limit to its universal cover and applying Hamilton's strong maximum principle, we deduce that the pull-back of the new limit on the universal cover splits off a line for all time \( t \leq  0 \) . Thus by combining with Theorem 6.2.2 and the argument in the proof of Lemma 6.4.1, we further deduce that the new limit is either the round cylinder \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) or the round \( {\mathbb{{RP}}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) . Since \( \bar{M} \) is orientable, the new limit must be \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) . Since \( \left( {\bar{M},{\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( {x,0}\right) }\right) \) has nonnegative curvature operator and the points \( \left\{  {x}_{j}\right\} \) going to infinity and \( \bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right)  \rightarrow   + \infty \) , this gives a contradiction to Proposition 6.1.1. So we have proved that the limiting gradient shrinking soliton has bounded curvature at each time.

Hence by Lemma 6.4.1, the limiting gradient shrinking soliton is either the round three-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3} \) or its metric quotients, or the infinite cylinder \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) or one of its \( {\mathbb{Z}}_{2} \) quotients. If the asymptotic gradient shrinking soliton is the round three-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3} \) or its metric quotients, it follows from Lemma 5.2.4 and Proposition 5.2.5 that the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution must be round. Thus in the following we may assume the asymptotic gradient shrinking soliton is the infinite cylinder \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) or a \( {\mathbb{Z}}_{2} \) quotient of \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) .

We now come back to consider the original ancient \( \kappa \) -solution \( \left( {M,{g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) . By rescaling, we can assume that \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  1 \) for all \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) satisfying \( {d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {x, p}\right)  \leq  2 \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - 1,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . We will argue as in the proof of Theorem 3.3.2 (Perelman’s no local collapsing theorem I) to obtain a positive lower bound for \( {\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {p,1}\right) }\right) \) .

Denote by \( \xi  = {\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}{\left( {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( p,1\right) \right) }^{\frac{1}{3}} \) . For any \( v \in  {T}_{p}M \) we can find an \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic \( \gamma \left( \tau \right) \) , starting at \( p \) , with \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}\sqrt{\tau }\dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right)  = v \) . It follows from the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic equation (3.2.1) that

\[
\frac{d}{d\tau }\left( {\sqrt{\tau }\dot{\gamma }}\right)  - \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\tau }\nabla R + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {\sqrt{\tau }\dot{\gamma }, \cdot  }\right)  = 0.
\]

By integrating as before we see that for \( \tau  \leq  \xi \) with the property \( \gamma \left( \sigma \right)  \in  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {p,1}\right) \) as long as \( \sigma  < \tau \) , there holds

\[
\left| {\sqrt{\tau }\dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right)  - v}\right|  \leq  {C\xi }\left( {\left| v\right|  + 1}\right)
\]

where \( C \) is some positive constant depending only on the dimension. Without loss of generality, we may assume \( {C\xi } \leq  \frac{1}{4} \) and \( \xi  \leq  \frac{1}{100} \) . Then for \( v \in  {T}_{p}M \) with \( \left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\xi }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) and for \( \tau  \leq  \xi \) with the property \( \gamma \left( \sigma \right)  \in  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {p,1}\right) \) as long as \( \sigma  < \tau \) , we have

\[
{d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {p,\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right)  \leq  {\int }_{0}^{\tau }\left| {\dot{\gamma }\left( \sigma \right) }\right| {d\sigma }
\]

\[
< \frac{1}{2}{\xi }^{-\frac{1}{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\tau }\frac{d\sigma }{\sqrt{\sigma }}
\]

\[
= 1\text{ . }
\]

This shows

(6.4.11)

\[
\mathcal{L}\exp \left\{  {\left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\xi }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right\}  \left( \xi \right)  \subset  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {p,1}\right) .
\]

We decompose Perelman’s reduced volume \( \widetilde{V}\left( \xi \right) \) as

(6.4.12)

\[
\widetilde{V}\left( \xi \right)  = {\int }_{\mathcal{L}\exp \left\{  {\left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\xi }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right\}  \left( \xi \right) }
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{M \smallsetminus  \mathcal{L}\exp \left\{  {\left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\xi }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right\}  \left( \xi \right) }{\left( 4\pi \xi \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,\xi }\right) }\right) d{V}_{{t}_{0} - \xi }\left( q\right) .
\]

By using (6.4.11) and the metric evolution equation of the Ricci flow, the first term on the RHS of (6.4.12) can be estimated by

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{L}\exp \left\{  {\left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\xi }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right\}  \left( \xi \right) }{\left( 4\pi \xi \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,\xi }\right) }\right) d{V}_{{t}_{0} - \xi }\left( q\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {\int }_{{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {p,1}\right) }{\left( 4\pi \xi \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}{e}^{3\xi }d{V}_{{t}_{0}}\left( q\right)
\]

\[
= {\left( 4\pi \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}{e}^{3\xi }{\xi }^{\frac{3}{2}}
\]

\[
< {\xi }^{\frac{3}{2}}\text{ , }
\]

while by using Theorem 3.2.7 (Perelman's Jacobian comparison theorem), the second term on the RHS of (6.4.12) can be estimated by

(6.4.13)

\[
{\int }_{M \smallsetminus  \mathcal{L}\exp \left\{  {\left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\xi }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right\}  \left( \xi \right) }{\left( 4\pi \xi \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,\xi }\right) }\right) d{V}_{{t}_{0} - \xi }\left( q\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {\int }_{\left\{  \left| v\right|  > \frac{1}{4}{\xi }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right\}  }{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}{\left. \exp \left( -l\left( \tau \right) \right) \mathcal{J}\left( \tau \right) \right| }_{\tau  = 0}{dv}
\]

\[
= {\left( 4\pi \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}{\int }_{\left\{  \left| v\right|  > \frac{1}{4}{\xi }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right\}  }\exp \left( {-{\left| v\right| }^{2}}\right) {dv}
\]

\[
< {\xi }^{\frac{3}{2}}
\]

since \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}{\tau }^{-\frac{3}{2}}\mathcal{J}\left( \tau \right)  = 1 \) and \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}l\left( \tau \right)  = {\left| v\right| }^{2} \) by (3.2.18) and (3.2.19) respectively. Thus we obtain

(6.4.14)

\[
\widetilde{V}\left( \xi \right)  < 2{\xi }^{\frac{3}{2}}.
\]

On the other hand, we recall that there exist a sequence \( {\tau }_{k} \rightarrow   + \infty \) and a sequence of points \( q\left( {\tau }_{k}\right)  \in  M \) with \( l\left( {q\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) ,{\tau }_{k}}\right)  \leq  \frac{3}{2} \) so that the scalings of the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution at \( q\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) \) with factor \( {\tau }_{k}^{-1} \) converge to either round \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) or one of its \( {\mathbb{Z}}_{2} \) quotients. For sufficiently large \( k \) , we construct a path \( \gamma  : \;\left\lbrack  {0,2{\tau }_{k}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M \) , connecting \( p \) to any given point \( q \in  M \) , as follows: the first half path \( {\left. \gamma \right| }_{\left\lbrack  0,{\tau }_{k}\right\rbrack  } \) connects \( p \) to \( q\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) \) such that

\[
l\left( {q\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) ,{\tau }_{k}}\right)  = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{{\tau }_{k}}}{\int }_{0}^{{\tau }_{k}}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {R + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau } \leq  2,
\]

and the second half path \( {\left. \gamma \right| }_{\left\lbrack  {\tau }_{k},2{\tau }_{k}\right\rbrack  } \) is a shortest geodesic connecting \( q\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) \) to \( q \) with respect to the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( {{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{k}}\right) \) . Note that the rescaled metric \( {\tau }_{k}^{-1}{g}_{ij}\left( {{t}_{0} - \tau }\right) \) over the domain \( {B}_{{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{k}}\left( {q\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) ,\sqrt{{\tau }_{k}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - 2{\tau }_{k},{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{k}}\right\rbrack \) is sufficiently close to the round

\( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) or its \( {\mathbb{Z}}_{2} \) quotients. Then there is a universal positive constant \( \beta \) such that

\[
l\left( {q,2{\tau }_{k}}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2{\tau }_{k}}}\left( {{\int }_{0}^{{\tau }_{k}} + {\int }_{{\tau }_{k}}^{2{\tau }_{k}}}\right) \sqrt{\tau }\left( {R + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau }
\]

\[
\leq  \sqrt{2} + \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2{\tau }_{k}}}{\int }_{{\tau }_{k}}^{2{\tau }_{k}}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {R + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau }
\]

\[
\leq  \beta
\]

for all \( q \in  {B}_{{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{k}}\left( {q\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) ,\sqrt{{\tau }_{k}}}\right) \) . Thus

\[
\widetilde{V}\left( {2{\tau }_{k}}\right)  = {\int }_{M}{\left( 4\pi \left( 2{\tau }_{k}\right) \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,2{\tau }_{k}}\right) }\right) d{V}_{{t}_{0} - 2{\tau }_{k}}\left( q\right)
\]

\[
\geq  {e}^{-\beta }{\int }_{{B}_{{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{k}}\left( {q\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) ,\sqrt{{\tau }_{k}}}\right) }{\left( 4\pi \left( 2{\tau }_{k}\right) \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}d{V}_{{t}_{0} - 2{\tau }_{k}}\left( q\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \widetilde{\beta }
\]

for some universal positive constant \( \widetilde{\beta } \) . Here we have used the curvature estimate (6.2.6). By combining with the monotonicity of Perelman's reduced volume (Theorem 3.2.8) and (6.4.14), we deduce that

\[
\widetilde{\beta } \leq  \widetilde{V}\left( {2{\tau }_{k}}\right)  \leq  \widetilde{V}\left( \xi \right)  < 2{\xi }^{\frac{3}{2}}.
\]

This proves

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {p,1}\right) }\right)  \geq  {\kappa }_{0} > 0
\]

for some universal positive constant \( {\kappa }_{0} \) . So we have proved that the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution is also an ancient \( {\kappa }_{0} \) -solution. \( \square \)

knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
First, the only nonflat oriented nonnegatively curved gradient shrinking 2-D soliton is the round \( {S}^{2} \) . The reference [30] given in I.11.3 for this fact does not actually cover it, as the reference only deals with compact solitons. A proof using Proposition 39.1 to rule out the noncompact case appears in [68].

Given this, the limit solution in Proposition 39.1 is a shrinking round 2-sphere. Thus the rescalings \( {\bar{\tau }}_{i}^{-1}g\left( {{t}_{0} - {\bar{\tau }}_{i}}\right) \) converge to a round 2-sphere as \( i \rightarrow  \infty \) . However, by [30] the Ricci flow makes an almost-round 2-sphere become more round. Thus any given time slice of the original \( \kappa \) -solution must be a round 2-sphere.

knowledge_statements.title: Regular-Value Submanifolds
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular-Value Submanifolds
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
(Inverse image of a regular value). Before discussing the next example, we need some definitions.

Let \( F : U \subset  {\mathrm{R}}^{n} \rightarrow  {\mathrm{R}}^{m} \) be a differentiable mapping of an open set \( U \) of \( {\mathbf{R}}^{n} \) . A point \( p \in  U \) is defined to be a critical point of \( F \) if the differential \( d{F}_{p} : {\mathbf{R}}^{n} \rightarrow  {\mathbf{R}}^{m} \) is not surjective. The image \( F\left( p\right) \) of a critical point is called a critical value of \( F \) . A point \( a \in  {\mathbf{R}}^{m} \) that is not a critical value is said to be a regular value of \( F \) . Note that any point \( a \notin  F\left( U\right) \) is trivially a regular value of \( F \) and that if there exists a regular value of \( F \) in \( {\mathbf{R}}^{m} \) , then \( n \geq  m \) .

Now let \( a \in  F\left( U\right) \) be a regular value of \( F \) . We are going to show that the inverse image \( {F}^{-1}\left( a\right)  \subset  {\mathbf{R}}^{n} \) is a regular surface of dimension \( n - m = k \) . From what was seen in Example 4.2, \( {F}^{-1}\left( a\right) \) is then a submanifold of \( {\mathbf{R}}^{n} \) .

To prove the assertion we use, again, the inverse function theorem. Let \( p \in  {F}^{-1}\left( a\right) \) . Denote by \( q = \left( {{y}_{1},\ldots ,{y}_{m},{x}_{1},\ldots {x}_{k}}\right) \) an arbitrary point of \( {\mathbf{R}}^{n = m + k} \) and by \( F\left( q\right)  = \left( {{f}_{1}\left( q\right) ,\ldots ,{f}_{m}\left( q\right) }\right) \) its image by the mapping \( F \) . Since \( a \) is a regular value of \( F, d{F}_{p} \) is surjective. Therefore, we can suppose that

\[
\frac{\partial \left( {{f}_{1},\ldots ,{f}_{m}}\right) }{\partial \left( {{y}_{1},\ldots ,{y}_{m}}\right) }\left( p\right)  \neq  0.
\]

Define a mapping \( \varphi  : U \subset  {\mathbf{R}}^{n} \rightarrow  {\mathbf{R}}^{n = m + k} \) by

\[
\varphi \left( {{y}_{1},\ldots ,{y}_{m},{x}_{1},\ldots ,{x}_{k}}\right)  = \left( {{f}_{1}\left( q\right) ,\ldots ,{f}_{m}\left( q\right) ,{x}_{1},\ldots ,{x}_{k}}\right) .
\]

Then

\[
\det {\left( d\varphi \right) }_{p} = \frac{\partial \left( {{f}_{1},\ldots ,{f}_{m}}\right) }{\partial \left( {{y}_{1},\ldots ,{y}_{m}}\right) }\left( p\right)  \neq  0.
\]

By the inverse function theorem, \( \varphi \) is a diffeomorphism of a neighborhood \( Q \) of \( p \) onto a neighborhood \( W \) of \( \varphi \left( p\right) \) . Let \( {K}^{m + k} \subset  W \subset \; {R}^{m + k} \) be a cube of center \( \varphi \left( p\right) \) and put \( V = {\varphi }^{-1}\left( {K}^{m + k}\right)  \cap  Q \) . Then \( \varphi \) maps the neighborhood \( V \) diffeomorphically onto \( {K}^{m + k} = {K}^{m} \times  {K}^{k} \) . Define a mapping \( \mathbf{x} : {K}^{k} \rightarrow  V \) by

\[
\mathbf{x}\left( {{x}_{1},\ldots ,{x}_{k}}\right)  = {\varphi }^{-1}\left( {{a}_{1},\ldots ,{a}_{m},{x}_{1},\ldots ,{x}_{k}}\right) ,
\]

where \( \left( {{a}_{1},\ldots ,{a}_{m}}\right)  = a \) . It is easy to check that \( \varphi \) satisfies conditions (a) and (b) of the definition of regular surface given in Example 4.2. Since \( p \) is arbitrary, \( {F}^{-1}\left( a\right) \) is a regular surface in \( {\mathbf{R}}^{n} \) , as asserted.

Before going on to other examples of differentiable manifolds, we should introduce the important global notion of orientation.

knowledge_statements.title: Real Projective Space as an Antipodal Quotient
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Real Projective Space as an Antipodal Quotient
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
(Another description of projective space). The set \( {P}^{n}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) of lines of \( {\mathbf{R}}^{n + 1} \) that pass through the origin can be thought of as the quotient space of the unit sphere \( {S}^{n} = \left\{  {p \in  {\mathbf{R}}^{n + 1};\left| p\right|  = 1}\right\} \) by the equivalence relation that identifies \( p \in  {S}^{n} \) with its antipodal point, \( A\left( p\right)  =  - p \) . Indeed, each line that passes through the origin determines two antipodal points and the correspondence so obtained is evidently bijective.

Taking into account this fact, we are going to introduce another differentiable structure on \( {P}^{n}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) (Cf. Example 2.4). For this, we initially introduce on \( {S}^{n} \subset  {\mathbf{R}}^{n + 1} \) the structure of a regular surface, defining parametrizations

\[
{\mathbf{x}}_{i}^{ + } : {U}_{i} \rightarrow  {S}^{n},\;{\mathbf{x}}_{i}^{ - } : {U}_{i} \rightarrow  {S}^{n},\;i = 1,\ldots , n + 1,
\]

in the following way:

\[
{U}_{i} = \left\{  {\left( {{x}_{1},\ldots ,{x}_{n + 1}}\right)  \in  {\mathbf{R}}^{n + 1};{x}_{i} = 0,}\right.
\]

\[
\left. {{x}_{1}^{2} + \ldots  + {x}_{i - 1}^{2} + {x}_{i + 1}^{2} + \ldots  + {x}_{n + 1}^{2} < 1}\right\}
\]

\[
{\mathbf{x}}_{i}^{ + }\left( {{x}_{1},\ldots ,{x}_{i - 1},{x}_{i + 1},\ldots ,{x}_{n + 1}}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {{x}_{1},\ldots ,{x}_{i - 1},{D}_{i},{x}_{i + 1},\ldots ,{x}_{n + 1}}\right) ,
\]

\[
{\mathbf{x}}_{i}^{ - }\left( {{x}_{1},\ldots ,{x}_{i - 1},{x}_{i + 1},\ldots ,{x}_{n + 1}}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {{x}_{1},\ldots ,{x}_{i - 1}, - {D}_{i},{x}_{i + 1},\ldots ,{x}_{n + 1}}\right) ,
\]

where \( {D}_{i} = \sqrt{1 - \left( {{x}_{1}^{2} + \ldots  + {x}_{i - 1}^{2} + {x}_{i + 1}^{2} + \ldots  + {x}_{n + 1}^{2}}\right) } \) . It is easy to verify that conditions (a) and (b) of the definition in Example 4.2 are satisfied. Therefore, the family

\[
\left\{  {\left( {{U}_{i},{\mathbf{x}}_{i}^{ + }}\right) ,\left( {{U}_{i},{\mathbf{x}}_{i}^{ - }}\right) }\right\}  ,\;i = 1,\ldots , n + 1
\]

is a differentiable structure on \( {S}^{n} \) . Geometrically, this is equivalent to covering the sphere \( {S}^{n} \) with coordinate neighborhoods that are hemi-spheres perpendicular to the axes \( {x}_{i} \) and taking as coordinates on, for example, \( {\mathbf{x}}_{i}^{ + }\left( {U}_{i}\right) \) , the coordinates of the orthogonal projection of \( {\mathbf{x}}_{i}^{ + }\left( {U}_{i}\right) \) on the hyperplane \( {x}_{i} = 0 \) (Fig. 10).

![019eafa4-c1ab-71ca-a069-1af7cc3160f3_35_495_1395_781_763_0.jpg](images/019eafa4-c1ab-71ca-a069-1af7cc3160f3_35_495_1395_781_763_0.jpg)

Figure 10

Let \( \pi  : {S}^{n} \rightarrow  {P}^{n}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) be the canonical projection, that is, \( \pi \left( p\right)  = \{ p, - p\} \) ; observe that \( \pi \left( {{\mathbf{x}}_{i}^{ + }\left( {U}_{i}\right) }\right)  = \pi \left( {{\mathbf{x}}_{i}^{ - }\left( {U}_{i}\right) }\right) \) . We are going to define a mapping \( {\mathbf{y}}_{i} : {U}_{i} \rightarrow  {P}^{n}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) by

\[
{\mathbf{y}}_{i} = \pi  \circ  {\mathbf{x}}_{i}^{ + }.
\]

Since \( \pi \) restricted to \( {\mathbf{x}}_{i}^{ + }\left( {U}_{i}\right) \) is one-to-one, we have that

\[
{\mathbf{y}}_{i}^{-1} \circ  {\mathbf{y}}_{j} = {\left( \pi  \circ  {\mathbf{x}}_{i}^{ + }\right) }^{-1} \circ  \left( {\pi  \circ  {\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{ + }}\right)  = {\left( {\mathbf{x}}_{i}^{ + }\right) }^{-1} \circ  {\mathbf{x}}_{j}^{ + },
\]

which yields the differentiability of \( {\mathbf{y}}_{i}^{-1} \circ  {\mathbf{y}}_{j} \) , for all \( i, j = 1,\ldots , n + 1 \) . Thus the family \( \left\{  \left( {{U}_{i},{y}_{i}}\right. \right. \) is a differentiable structure for \( {P}^{n}\left( \mathrm{R}\right) \) .

In fact, this differentiable structure and that of Example 2.4 give rise to the same maximal structure. Indeed, the coordinate neighborhoods are the same and the change of coordinates are given by:

\[
\left( {\frac{{x}_{1}}{{x}_{i}},\ldots ,\frac{{x}_{i - 1}}{{x}_{i}},1,\frac{{x}_{i + 1}}{{x}_{i}},\ldots ,\frac{{x}_{n + 1}}{{x}_{i}}}\right)  \leftrightarrow
\]

\[
\leftrightarrow  \left( {{x}_{1},\ldots ,{x}_{i - 1},{D}_{i},{x}_{i + 1},\ldots ,{x}_{n + 1}}\right)
\]

which, since \( {x}_{i} \neq  0 \) and \( {D}_{i} \neq  0 \) , is differentiable.

As we shall see in Exercise 9, \( {P}^{n}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) is orientable if and only if \( n \) is odd.

children.title: Compact Ricci Solitons Are Gradient

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Ricci Solitons Are Gradient
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact Ricci Solitons Are Gradient
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The goal of this problem is to show that every compact Ricci soliton is a gradient Ricci soliton. This was first proved by G. Perelman [68]. Let \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) be a compact Riemannian manifold of dimension \( n \geq  3 \) , and let \( \rho \) be a positive real number. By the previous problem, we can find a real number \( \mu \) and a positive function \( \varphi  \in  {C}^{\infty }\left( M\right) \) such that

\[
{\Delta }_{g}\varphi  = \left( {\frac{1}{4}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g} - \rho \log \varphi  - \mu }\right) \varphi .
\]

(i) Consider the tensor \( H = {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g} + {D}^{2}f - {\rho g} \) , where \( f =  - 2\log \varphi \) . Show that

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, j = 1}}^{n}{g}^{ij}{D}_{j}\left( {{e}^{-f}{H}_{ik}}\right)  = 0.
\]

(ii) Suppose that \( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g} + \frac{1}{2}{\mathcal{L}}_{\xi }g = {\rho g} \) for some vector field \( \xi \) . Show that

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, j, k = 1}}^{n}{g}^{ij}{D}_{j}\left( {{e}^{-f}{H}_{ik}\left( {{\partial }^{k}f - {\xi }^{k}}\right) }\right)  = {e}^{-f}{\left| H\right| }^{2}.
\]

Deduce from this that \( H = 0 \) .

knowledge_statements.title: Hypersurfaces and the Shape Operator
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hypersurfaces and the Shape Operator
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the particular case in which the codi-mension of the immersion is 1, i.e., \( f : {M}^{n} \rightarrow  {\bar{M}}^{n + 1};f\left( M\right)  \subset  \bar{M} \) is then called a hypersurface. (Observe that a hypersurface can have self-intersections).

Let \( p \in  M \) and \( \eta  \in  {\left( {T}_{p}M\right) }^{ \bot  },\left| \eta \right|  = 1 \) . Since \( {S}_{\eta } : {T}_{p}M \rightarrow \; {T}_{p}M \) is symmetric, there exists an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) of \( {T}_{p}M \) with real eigenvalues \( {\lambda }_{1},\ldots ,{\lambda }_{n} \) , i.e., \( {S}_{\eta }\left( {e}_{i}\right)  = \; {\lambda }_{i}{e}_{i},1 \leq  i \leq  n \) . If \( M \) and \( \bar{M} \) are both orientable and oriented (i.e., orientations are chosen on \( M \) and \( \bar{M} \) ) then the vector \( \eta \) is uniquely determined if we require that both \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) is a basis in the orientation of \( M \) , and \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n},\eta }\right\} \) is a basis in the orientation of \( \bar{M} \) . In this case, we say that the \( {e}_{i} \) are principal directions and that the \( {\lambda }_{i} = {k}_{i} \) are principal curvatures of \( f \) . The symmetric functions of \( {\lambda }_{1},\ldots ,{\lambda }_{n} \) are invariants of the immersion. For example: \( \det \left( {S}_{\eta }\right)  = {\lambda }_{1}\ldots {\lambda }_{n} \) is called the Gauss-Kronecker curvature of \( f \) and \( \frac{1}{n}\left( {{\lambda }_{1} + \cdots  + {\lambda }_{n}}\right) \) is called the mean curvature of \( f \) .

An important case occurs when \( \bar{M} = {\mathbf{R}}^{n + 1} \) . Here, we can give an interesting geometric interpretation of \( {S}_{\eta } \) . To begin with, let \( N \) be a local extension of \( \eta \) , which is a unit vector field normal to \( M \) . Let \( {S}_{1}^{n} = \left\{  {x \in  {\mathbf{R}}^{n + 1};\left| x\right|  = 1}\right\} \) be the unit sphere in \( {\mathbf{R}}^{n + 1} \) and define the Gauss spherical mapping, \( g : {M}^{n} \rightarrow  {S}_{1}^{n} \) , by translating the origin of the field \( N \) to the origin of \( {\mathbf{R}}^{n + 1} \) and taking

\[
g\left( q\right)  = \text{ endpoint of the translation of }N\left( q\right) \text{ . }
\]

Since \( {T}_{q}M \) and \( {T}_{g\left( q\right) }{S}_{1}^{n} \) are parallel, we can identify them, and see that \( d{g}_{q} : {T}_{q}M \rightarrow  {T}_{q}M \) is given by

\[
d{g}_{q}\left( x\right)  = \frac{d}{dt}{\left( N \circ  c\left( t\right) \right) }_{t = 0} = {\bar{\nabla }}_{x}N = {\left( {\bar{\nabla }}_{x}N\right) }^{T} =  - {S}_{\eta }\left( x\right) ,
\]

where \( c : \left( {-\varepsilon ,\varepsilon }\right)  \rightarrow  M \) is a curve with \( c\left( 0\right)  = q,{c}^{\prime }\left( 0\right)  = x \) , and we have used the fact that \( \langle N, N\rangle  = 1 \) to guarantee that \( {\bar{\nabla }}_{x}N = {\left( {\bar{\nabla }}_{x}N\right) }^{T} \) . It follows that \( - {S}_{\eta } \) is the derivative of the Gauss spherical mapping.

The Gauss mapping has important topological implications. As an example, we shall prove the following fact: Let \( {M}^{n}, n \geq \) 2, be a connected, compact, orientable manifold. If there exists an immersion \( f : {M}^{n} \rightarrow  {\mathbf{R}}^{n + 1} \) with non-vanishing Gauss-Kronecker curvature at every point of \( M \) , then \( M \) is diffeomorphic to \( {S}_{1}^{n} \) . The proof depends on the properties of covering spaces (see for example, M. do Carmo \( \left\lbrack  {dC2}\right\rbrack  §{5.6}) \) . The fact that \( \det \left( {d{g}_{p}}\right)  \neq  0 \) , for the Gauss mapping, tells us that \( g : M \rightarrow  {S}_{1}^{n} \) is a local diffeomorphism. Since \( M \) is compact, \( g \) is a covering map, and because \( {S}_{1}^{n} \) is simply connected, \( g \) is a diffeomorphism.

We now relate the curvature of \( M \) with the curvature of \( \bar{M} \) and the second fundamental forms. If \( x, y \in  {T}_{p}M \subset  {T}_{p}\bar{M} \) , are linearly independent, denote by \( K\left( {x, y}\right) \) and \( \bar{K}\left( {x, y}\right) \) the sectional curvatures of \( M \) and \( \bar{M} \) , respectively, in the plane generated by \( x \) and \( y \) . Another proof of the next theorem will come up in Section 3 of this chapter.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bochner Formula for Harmonic Two-Forms
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
This problem is concerned with the Bochner formula for harmonic two-forms (cf. [61]; see also [59]). Let \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) be a compact Riemannian manifold of dimension \( n \geq  4 \) , and let \( \psi \) be a harmonic two-form on \( M \) .

(i) Show that

\[
\Delta {\psi }_{ik} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{n}{\operatorname{Ric}}_{i}^{j}{\psi }_{jk} + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{n}{\operatorname{Ric}}_{k}^{j}{\psi }_{ij} - 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j, l = 1}}^{n}{R}_{ijkl}{\psi }^{jl}.
\]

(ii) Suppose that \( n \) is even and \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature. Show that \( \psi \) is parallel.

(iii) Suppose that \( n \) is odd and the curvature tensor of \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) lies in the cone \( \widetilde{C} \) for all points \( p \in  M \) . Show that \( \psi \) is parallel.

knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
In view of condition (iii), \( \widehat{R} \) lies in the interior of the PIC cone. Therefore, the assertion is true for \( \widehat{b} = 0 \) . Hence, it suffices to consider the case \( 0 < \widehat{b} \leq  \delta {e}^{-8\widehat{t}} \) . Let us define functions \( a\left( t\right) , b\left( t\right) \) by \( b\left( t\right)  = {e}^{8\left( {\widehat{t} - t}\right) }\widehat{b} \) and \( a\left( t\right)  = {2b}\left( t\right)  + \left( {n - 2}\right) b{\left( t\right) }^{2} \) . Moreover, let \( S\left( t\right)  \mathrel{\text{ := }} {\ell }_{a\left( t\right) , b\left( t\right) }^{-1}\left( {R\left( t\right) }\right) \) . Since condition (i) holds up to time \( \widehat{t} \) , we know that \( S\left( t\right)  \in \) PIC for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\widehat{t}}\right\rbrack \) . The evolution of \( S\left( t\right) \) is given by

\[
{\left. \frac{d}{dt}S\left( t\right) \right| }_{t = \widehat{t}} = Q\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + {D}_{\widehat{a},\widehat{b}}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  - {b}^{\prime }\left( \widehat{t}\right) U = Q\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + {D}_{\widehat{a},\widehat{b}}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + 8\widehat{b}U,
\]

where

\[
U = \frac{1}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) \widehat{b}}\operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
- \frac{1}{n}\left( {\frac{1}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) \widehat{b}} - \frac{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) \widehat{b}}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \widehat{a}}}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \text{ id } \oslash  \text{ id. }
\]

We claim that \( {D}_{\widehat{a},\widehat{b}}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + 8\widehat{b}U \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{\widehat{S}} \) PIC. To verify this, we distinguish two cases:

Case 1: Suppose first that \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \) is strictly two-positive. By Lemma A.2, \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \) lies in the interior of the PIC cone. Since \( 2\widehat{a} = 2\widehat{b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {\widehat{b}}^{2} \) , this implies that \( {D}_{\widehat{a},\widehat{b}}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \) lies in the interior of the PIC cone. Since \( U \in  {T}_{\widehat{S}} \) PIC by Lemma 2.5, it follows that \( {D}_{\widehat{a},\widehat{b}}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + 8\widehat{b}U \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{\widehat{S}} \) PIC, as claimed.

Case 2: Suppose next that \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \) is not strictly two-positive. In this case, \( \operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \leq  C\left( n\right) \left| {\mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\left( \widehat{S}\right) }\right| \) . Since \( 2\widehat{a} = 2\widehat{b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {\widehat{b}}^{2} \) , it follows that

\[
{D}_{\widehat{a},\widehat{b}}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  - 2\widehat{a}\operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  - 2{\widehat{b}}^{\frac{17}{8}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} \in  \mathrm{{PIC}}
\]

if \( \widehat{b} > 0 \) is sufficiently small. Condition (ii) implies \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + \left( {1 + {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{5}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) }\right) \) id is weakly two-positive. Using Lemma A.2, we obtain

\[
2\widehat{a}\operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)
\]

\[
+ 4\widehat{a}\left( {1 + {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{5}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) }\right) \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} + 4\widehat{a}\left( {1 + {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{5}{2}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }^{2}}\right) \mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
= 2\widehat{a}\left\lbrack  {\operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + \left( {1 + {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{5}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) }\right) \mathrm{{id}}}\right\rbrack   \oslash  \left\lbrack  {\operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + \left( {1 + {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{5}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) }\right) \mathrm{{id}}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
+ 2\widehat{a}{\left( 1 - {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{5}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \right) }^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} \in  \text{ PIC. }
\]

On the other hand, Lemma 2.6 gives

\[
8\widehat{b}U - 4\widehat{a}\operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} - 4\widehat{a}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} + {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{17}{8}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} \in  {T}_{\widehat{S}}\mathrm{{PIC}}\text{ . }
\]

Moreover, if \( \widehat{b} > 0 \) is sufficiently small, then \( \widehat{a}{\widehat{b}}^{\frac{5}{4}} \) is much smaller than \( {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{17}{8}} \) . Since \( \left| {\operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) }\right|  \leq  C\left( n\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \) , it follows that

\[
{\widehat{b}}^{\frac{17}{8}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} - 4\widehat{a}{\widehat{b}}^{\frac{5}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} - 4\widehat{a}{\widehat{b}}^{\frac{5}{2}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

lies in the interior of the PIC cone. Adding all four formulae, we conclude that \( {D}_{\widehat{a},\widehat{b}}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + 8\widehat{b}U \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{\widehat{S}} \) PIC.

To summarize, we have shown that \( {D}_{\widehat{a},\widehat{b}}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + 8\widehat{b}U \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{\widehat{S}} \) PIC. Since \( Q\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \in  {T}_{\widehat{S}} \) PIC by Proposition 7.5 in [5], we conclude that \( {\left. \frac{d}{dt}S\left( t\right) \right| }_{t = \widehat{t}} \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{\widehat{S}} \) PIC. Hence, if \( \widehat{S} \) lies on the boundary of the PIC cone, then \( S\left( t\right) \) lies outside the PIC cone if \( t \in  \lbrack 0,\widehat{t}) \) is sufficiently close to \( \widehat{t} \) . This is a contradiction. This completes the proof of Lemma 2.7.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: (Hamilton’s advanced maximum principle [59]). Let \( K \) be a closed subset of \( V \) satisfying the hypothesis (H1) and (H2). Suppose that for any \( x \in  M \) and any initial time \( {t}_{0} \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , any solution \( {\sigma }_{x}\left( t\right) \) of the (ODE) which starts in \( {K}_{x} \) at \( {t}_{0} \) will remain in \( {K}_{x} \) for all later times. Then for any initial time \( {t}_{0} \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) the solution \( \sigma \left( {x, t}\right) \) of the (PDE) will remain in \( K \) for all later times provided \( \sigma \left( {x, t}\right) \) starts in \( K \) at time \( {t}_{0} \) and \( \sigma \left( {x, t}\right) \) is uniformly bounded with respect to the bundle metric \( {h}_{ab} \) on \( M \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right\rbrack \) .

knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
Since the solution \( \sigma \left( {x, t}\right) \) of the (PDE) is uniformly bounded with respect to the bundle metric \( {h}_{ab} \) on \( M \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right\rbrack \) by hypothesis, we may assume that \( K \) is contained in a tubular neighborhood \( V\left( r\right) \) of the zero section in \( V \) whose intersection with each fiber \( {V}_{x} \) is a ball of radius \( r \) around the origin measured by the bundle metric \( {h}_{ab} \) for some large \( r > 0 \) .

Recall that \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , is a smooth solution to the Ricci flow with uniformly bounded curvature on \( M \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . From Lemma 2.1.1, we have a smooth function \( f \) such that \( f \geq  1 \) everywhere, \( f\left( x\right)  \rightarrow   + \infty \) as \( {d}_{0}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  \rightarrow   + \infty \) for some fixed point \( {x}_{0} \in  M \) , and the first and second covariant derivatives with respect to the metrics \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) are uniformly bounded on \( M \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Using the metric \( {h}_{ab} \) in each fiber \( {V}_{x} \) and writing \( \left| {\varphi  - \eta }\right| \) for the distance between \( \varphi  \in  {V}_{x} \) and \( \eta  \in  {V}_{x} \) , we set

\[
s\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\left\{  {\inf \left\{  {\left| {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right|  \mid  \eta  \in  {K}_{x} \triangleq  K \cap  {V}_{x}}\right\}   - \epsilon {e}^{At}f\left( x\right) }\right\}
\]

where \( \epsilon \) is an arbitrarily small positive number and \( A \) is a positive constant to be determined. We rewrite the function \( s\left( t\right) \) as

\[
s\left( t\right)  = \sup \left\{  {l\left( {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right)  - \epsilon {e}^{At}f\left( x\right)  \mid  x \in  M,\eta  \in  \partial {K}_{x}\text{ and }l \in  {S}_{\eta }{K}_{x}}\right\}  .
\]

By the construction of the function \( f \) , we see that the sup is taken in a compact subset of \( M \times  V \times  {V}^{ * } \) for all \( t \) . Then by Lemma 2.3.3,

(2.3.2)

\[
\frac{{ds}\left( t\right) }{dt} \leq  \sup \left\{  {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}l\left( {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right)  - {\epsilon A}{e}^{At}f\left( x\right) }\right\}
\]

where the sup is over all \( x \in  M,\eta  \in  \partial {K}_{x} \) and \( l \in  {S}_{\eta }{K}_{x} \) such that

\[
l\left( {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right)  - \epsilon {e}^{At}f\left( x\right)  = s\left( t\right) ;
\]

in particular we have \( \left| {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right|  = l\left( {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right) \) , where \( \eta \) is the unique closest point in \( {K}_{x} \) to \( \sigma \left( {x, t}\right) \) , and \( l \) is the linear function of length one on the fiber \( {V}_{x} \) with gradient in the direction of \( \eta \) to \( \sigma \left( {x, t}\right) \) . We compute at these \( \left( {x,\eta , l}\right) \) ,

(2.3.3)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}l\left( {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right)  - {\epsilon A}{e}^{At}f\left( x\right)
\]

\[
= l\left( \frac{\partial \sigma \left( {x, t}\right) }{\partial t}\right)  - {\epsilon A}{e}^{At}f\left( x\right)
\]

\[
= l\left( {{\Delta }_{t}\sigma \left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  + l\left( {{u}^{i}\left( {x, t}\right) {\left( {\nabla }_{t}\right) }_{i}\sigma \left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  + l\left( {N\left( {x,\sigma \left( {x, t}\right) , t}\right) }\right)  - {\epsilon A}{e}^{At}f\left( x\right) .
\]

By the assumption and Lemma 2.3.4 we have \( \eta  + N\left( {x,\eta , t}\right)  \in  {T}_{\eta }{K}_{x} \) . Hence, for those \( \left( {x,\eta , l}\right) , l\left( {N\left( {x,\eta , t}\right) }\right)  \leq  0 \) and then

(2.3.4)

\[
l\left( {N\left( {x,\sigma \left( {x, t}\right) , t}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\leq  l\left( {N\left( {x,\eta , t}\right) }\right)  + \left| {N\left( {x,\sigma \left( {x, t}\right) , t}\right)  - N\left( {x,\eta , t}\right) }\right|
\]

\[
\leq  C\left| {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right|  = C\left( {s\left( t\right)  + \epsilon {e}^{At}f\left( x\right) }\right)
\]

for some positive constant \( C \) by the assumption that \( N\left( {x,\sigma , t}\right) \) is Lipschitz in \( \sigma \) and the fact that the sup is taken on a compact set. Thus the combination of (2.3.2)-(2.3.4) gives

(2.3.5)

\[
\frac{{ds}\left( t\right) }{dt} \leq  l\left( {{\Delta }_{t}\sigma \left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  + l\left( {{u}^{i}\left( {x, t}\right) {\left( {\nabla }_{t}\right) }_{i}\sigma \left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  + {Cs}\left( t\right)  + \epsilon \left( {C - A}\right) {e}^{At}f\left( x\right)
\]

for those \( x \in  M,\eta  \in  \partial {K}_{x} \) and \( l \in  {S}_{\eta }{K}_{x} \) such that \( l\left( {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right)  - \epsilon {e}^{At}f\left( x\right)  = s\left( t\right) \) .

Next we estimate the first two terms of (2.3.5). As we extend a vector in a bundle from a point \( x \) by parallel translation along geodesics emanating radially out of \( x \) , we will get a smooth section of the bundle in some small neighborhood of \( x \) such that all the symmetrized covariant derivatives at \( x \) are zero. Now let us extend \( \eta  \in  {V}_{x} \) and \( l \in  {V}_{x}^{ * } \) in this manner. Clearly, we continue to have \( \left| l\right| \left( \cdot \right)  = 1 \) . Since \( K \) is invariant under parallel translations, we continue to have \( \eta \left( \cdot \right)  \in  \partial K \) and \( l\left( \cdot \right) \) as a support function for \( K \) at \( \eta \left( \cdot \right) \) . Therefore

\[
l\left( {\sigma \left( {\cdot , t}\right)  - \eta \left( \cdot \right) }\right)  - \epsilon {e}^{At}f\left( \cdot \right)  \leq  s\left( t\right)
\]

in the neighborhood. It follows that the function \( l\left( {\sigma \left( {\cdot , t}\right)  - \eta \left( \cdot \right) }\right)  - \epsilon {e}^{At}f\left( \cdot \right) \) has a local maximum at \( x \) , so at \( x \)

\[
{\left( {\nabla }_{t}\right) }_{i}\left( {l\left( {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right)  - \epsilon {e}^{At}f\left( x\right) }\right)  = 0,
\]

\[
\text{ and }{\Delta }_{t}\left( {l\left( {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right)  - \epsilon {e}^{At}f\left( x\right) }\right)  \leq  0\text{ . }
\]

Hence at \( x \)

\[
l\left( {{\left( {\nabla }_{t}\right) }_{i}\sigma \left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  - \epsilon {e}^{At}{\left( {\nabla }_{t}\right) }_{i}f\left( x\right)  = 0,
\]

\[
\text{ and }l\left( {{\Delta }_{t}\sigma \left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  - \epsilon {e}^{At}{\Delta }_{t}f\left( x\right)  \leq  0\text{ . }
\]

Therefore by combining with (2.3.5), we have

\[
\frac{d}{dt}s\left( t\right)  \leq  {Cs}\left( t\right)  + \epsilon \left( {{\Delta }_{t}f\left( x\right)  + {u}^{i}{\left( {\nabla }_{t}\right) }_{i}f\left( x\right)  + \left( {C - A}\right) f\left( x\right) }\right) {e}^{At}
\]

\[
\leq  {Cs}\left( t\right)
\]

for \( A > 0 \) large enough, since \( f\left( x\right)  \geq  1 \) and the first and second covariant derivatives of \( f \) are uniformly bounded on \( M \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . So by applying Lemma 2.3.2 and the arbitrariness of \( \epsilon \) , we have completed the proof of Theorem 2.3.1. 0

knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
Suppose that the assertion is false. Then

\[
\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} + 2{b}^{\frac{5}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  =  - 2
\]

for some pair of orthonormal vectors \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2}}\right\} \) . We may assume that \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2}}\right\} \) are eigenvectors of \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \) , and \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} \geq  \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} \) . Let us extend \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2}}\right\} \) to an eigenbasis \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) of \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \) . Clearly, \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{pp} \geq  \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} \) for \( 3 \leq  p \leq  n \) . For each \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\widehat{t}}\right\rbrack \) , we define \( S\left( t\right)  \mathrel{\text{ := }} {l}_{a, b}^{-1}\left( {R\left( t\right) }\right) \) . Since condition (ii) holds up to time \( \widehat{t} \) , we know that

\[
\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\left( t\right) \right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\left( t\right) \right) }_{22} + 2{b}^{\frac{5}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( {S\left( t\right) }\right)  \geq   - 2
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\widehat{t}}\right\rbrack \) . The evolution of \( S\left( t\right) \) is given by \( {\left. \frac{d}{dt}S\left( t\right) \right| }_{t = \widehat{t}} = Q\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + {D}_{a, b}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \) . Using the formula for \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( \widehat{S}\right) }\right) \) , we obtain

\[
0 \geq  {\left. \frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\left( t\right) \right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\left( t\right) \right) }_{22} + 2{b}^{\frac{5}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\left( t\right) \right) \right) \right| }_{t = \widehat{t}}
\]

\[
\geq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 1}}^{n}\left( {{\widehat{S}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{S}}_{2p2p}}\right) \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{pp}
\]

\[
+ \frac{3}{2}{b}^{\frac{5}{4}}{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \right| }^{2} - {2b}\left( {{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }^{2}\right) }_{11} + {\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }^{2}\right) }_{22}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{4}{n}\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22}}\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\widehat{S}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{S}}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{pp} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22}}\right) }\right)  + \frac{3}{2}{b}^{\frac{5}{4}}{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \frac{1}{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) {\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22}\right) }^{2} - b{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \frac{4}{n}\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22}}\right)
\]

if \( b \geq  0 \) is sufficiently small. Note that \( {\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \right| }^{2} \geq  \frac{1}{n}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }^{2} \) . Hence, if \( b \geq  0 \) is sufficiently small, then

\[
\frac{1}{2}{b}^{\frac{5}{4}}{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \right| }^{2} + \frac{1}{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) {\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
>  - \frac{4}{n}\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22}}\right)
\]

by Young's inequality. This gives

\[
0 \geq  {\left. \frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\left( t\right) \right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\left( t\right) \right) }_{22} + 2{b}^{\frac{5}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\left( t\right) \right) \right) \right| }_{t = \widehat{t}}
\]

\[
> \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\widehat{S}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{S}}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{pp} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
+ {b}^{\frac{5}{4}}{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \right| }^{2} - b{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11}\right) }^{2}.
\]

At this point, we distinguish two cases:

Case 1: Suppose first that \( {\widehat{S}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{S}}_{2p2p} \geq  0 \) for all \( p \in  \{ 3,\ldots , n\} \) . In this case,

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\widehat{S}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{S}}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{pp} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{1}{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\widehat{S}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{S}}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11}}\right)
\]

hence

\[
0 \geq  {\left. \frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\left( t\right) \right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\left( t\right) \right) }_{22} + 2{b}^{\frac{5}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\left( t\right) \right) \right) \right| }_{t = \widehat{t}}
\]

\[
> \frac{1}{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\widehat{S}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{S}}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {b}^{\frac{5}{4}}{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \right| }^{2} - b{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11}\right) }^{2}
\]

If \( b = 0 \) or \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} \leq  {b}^{\frac{1}{8}}\left| {\operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) }\right| \) or \( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\widehat{S}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{S}}_{2p2p}}\right)  \geq \; {2b}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11}}\right) \) , then the right-hand side is nonnegative and we arrive at a contradiction. Therefore, we must have \( b > 0 \) and \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} \geq \; {b}^{\frac{1}{8}}\left| {\operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) }\right| \) and \( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\widehat{S}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{S}}_{2p2p}}\right)  \leq  {2b}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11}}\right) \) . Since \( \left| {\widehat{R} - \widehat{S}}\right| \; \leq  C\left( n\right) b\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{R}\right) \) , it follows that \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{R}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{R}\right) }_{11} \geq  c\left( n\right) {b}^{\frac{1}{8}}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{R}\right) \) and \( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\widehat{R}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{R}}_{2p2p}}\right)  \leq  C\left( n\right) b\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{R}\right) \) . On the other hand, using Lemma 2.4, we obtain

\[
{\widehat{R}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{R}}_{2p2p} + {\widehat{R}}_{1q1q} + {\widehat{R}}_{2q2q}
\]

\[
\geq  c\left( n\right) {b}^{\frac{1}{4}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \widehat{R}\right) }^{-3}{\left( \left| {\widehat{R}}_{1p1p}\right|  + \left| {\widehat{R}}_{2p2p}\right|  + \left| {\widehat{R}}_{1q1q}\right|  + \left| {\widehat{R}}_{2q2q}\right| \right) }^{4}
\]

for \( 3 \leq  p < q \leq  n \) . Summation over \( p \) and \( q \) gives

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\widehat{R}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{R}}_{2p2p}}\right)  \geq  c\left( n\right) {b}^{\frac{1}{4}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \widehat{R}\right) }^{-3}{\left( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( \left| {\widehat{R}}_{1p1p}\right|  + \left| {\widehat{R}}_{2p2p}\right| \right) \right) }^{4}
\]

\[
\geq  c\left( n\right) {b}^{\frac{1}{4}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \widehat{R}\right) }^{-3}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{R}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{R}\right) }_{11}\right) }^{4}
\]

\[
\geq  c\left( n\right) {b}^{\frac{3}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{R}\right) .
\]

This contradicts the inequality \( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\widehat{R}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{R}}_{2p2p}}\right)  \leq  C\left( n\right) b\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{R}\right) \) if \( b \) is sufficiently small.

Case 2: Suppose next that \( {\widehat{S}}_{1m1m} + {\widehat{S}}_{2m2m} < 0 \) for some \( m \in  \{ 3,\ldots , n\} \) . Since \( \widehat{S} \in \) PIC, Lemma A. 3 implies that each eigenvalue of \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \) is bounded from above by the sum of all the other eigenvalues. Therefore,

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p \in  \{ 1,\ldots , n\} \smallsetminus \{ m\} }}\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{pp} \geq  \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{mm}.
\]

Since \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} \leq  0 \) , it follows that

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p \in  \{ 3,\ldots , n\} \smallsetminus \{ m\} }}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{pp} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{mm} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22}}\right) .
\]

This implies

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{\widehat{S}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{S}}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{pp} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p \in  \{ 3,\ldots , n\} \smallsetminus \{ m\} }}\left( {{\widehat{S}}_{1m1m} + {\widehat{S}}_{2m2m} + {\widehat{S}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{S}}_{2p2p}}\right)
\]

\[
\cdot  \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{pp} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{1}{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p \in  \{ 3,\ldots , n\} \smallsetminus \{ m\} }}\left( {{\widehat{S}}_{1m1m} + {\widehat{S}}_{2m2m} + {\widehat{S}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{S}}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11}}\right) ,
\]

hence

\[
0 \geq  {\left. \frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\left( t\right) \right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\left( t\right) \right) }_{22} + 2{b}^{\frac{5}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\left( t\right) \right) \right) \right| }_{t = \widehat{t}}
\]

\[
> \frac{1}{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p \in  \{ 3,\ldots , n\} \smallsetminus \{ m\} }}\left( {{\widehat{S}}_{1m1m} + {\widehat{S}}_{2m2m} + {\widehat{S}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{S}}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {b}^{\frac{5}{4}}{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \right| }^{2} - b{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11}\right) }^{2}.
\]

If \( b = 0 \) or \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} \leq  {b}^{\frac{1}{8}}\left| {\operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) }\right| \) or

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p \in  \{ 3,\ldots , n\} \smallsetminus \{ m\} }}\left( {{\widehat{S}}_{1m1m} + {\widehat{S}}_{2m2m} + {\widehat{S}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{S}}_{2p2p}}\right)  \geq  {2b}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11}}\right) ,
\]

then the right-hand side is nonnegative, and we arrive at a contradiction. Therefore, we must have \( b > 0 \) and \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} \geq  {b}^{\frac{1}{8}}\left| {\operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) }\right| \) and

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p \in  \{ 3,\ldots , n\} \smallsetminus \{ m\} }}\left( {{\widehat{S}}_{1m1m} + {\widehat{S}}_{2m2m} + {\widehat{S}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{S}}_{2p2p}}\right)  \leq  {2b}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11}}\right) .
\]

Since \( \left| {\widehat{R} - \widehat{S}}\right|  \leq  C\left( n\right) b\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{R}\right) \) , it follows that

\[
\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{R}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{R}\right) }_{11} \geq  c\left( n\right) {b}^{\frac{1}{8}}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{R}\right)
\]

and

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p \in  \{ 3,\ldots , n\} \smallsetminus \{ m\} }}\left( {{\widehat{R}}_{1m1m} + {\widehat{R}}_{2m2m} + {\widehat{R}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{R}}_{2p2p}}\right)  \leq  C\left( n\right) b\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{R}\right) .
\]

On the other hand, using Lemma 2.4, we obtain

\[
{\widehat{R}}_{1m1m} + {\widehat{R}}_{2m2m} + {\widehat{R}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{R}}_{2p2p}
\]

\[
\operatorname{geqc}\left( n\right) {b}^{\frac{1}{4}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \widehat{R}\right) }^{-3}{\left( \left| {\widehat{R}}_{1m1m}\right|  + \left| {\widehat{R}}_{2m2m}\right|  + \left| {\widehat{R}}_{1p1p}\right|  + \left| {\widehat{R}}_{2p2p}\right| \right) }^{4}
\]

for \( p \in  \{ 3,\ldots , n\}  \smallsetminus  \{ m\} \) . Summation over \( p \in  \{ 3,\ldots , n\}  \smallsetminus  \{ m\} \) gives

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p \in  \{ 3,\ldots , n\} \smallsetminus \{ m\} }}\left( {{\widehat{R}}_{1m1m} + {\widehat{R}}_{2m2m} + {\widehat{R}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{R}}_{2p2p}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  c\left( n\right) {b}^{\frac{1}{4}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \widehat{R}\right) }^{-3}{\left( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( \left| {\widehat{R}}_{1p1p}\right|  + \left| {\widehat{R}}_{2p2p}\right| \right) \right) }^{4}
\]

\[
\geq  c\left( n\right) {b}^{\frac{1}{4}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \widehat{R}\right) }^{-3}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{R}\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{R}\right) }_{11}\right) }^{4}
\]

\[
\geq  c\left( n\right) {b}^{\frac{3}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{R}\right) .
\]

This contradicts the inequality

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p \in  \{ 3,\ldots , n\} \smallsetminus \{ m\} }}\left( {{\widehat{R}}_{1m1m} + {\widehat{R}}_{2m2m} + {\widehat{R}}_{1p1p} + {\widehat{R}}_{2p2p}}\right)  \leq  C\left( n\right) b\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{R}\right)
\]

if \( b \) is sufficiently small.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \( U \subset  {R}^{n} \) be an open set and \( Z \subset  U \) be a closed convex subset. Consider the ODE

(2.3.1)

\[
\frac{d\varphi }{dt} = N\left( {\varphi , t}\right)
\]

where \( N : U \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  {R}^{n} \) is continuous and Lipschitz in \( \varphi \) . Then the following two statements are equivalent.

(i) For any initial time \( {t}_{0} \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , any solution of the ODE (2.3.1) which starts in \( Z \) at \( {t}_{0} \) will remain in \( Z \) for all later times;

(ii) \( \varphi  + N\left( {\varphi , t}\right)  \in  {T}_{\varphi }Z \) for all \( \varphi  \in  \partial Z \) and \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) .

We say that a linear function \( l \) on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) is a support function for \( Z \) at \( \varphi  \in  \partial Z \) and write \( l \in  {S}_{\varphi }Z \) if \( \left| l\right|  = 1 \) and \( l\left( \varphi \right)  \geq  l\left( \eta \right) \) for all \( \eta  \in  Z \) . Then \( \varphi  + N\left( {\varphi , t}\right)  \in  {T}_{\varphi }Z \) if and only if \( l\left( {N\left( {\varphi , t}\right) }\right)  \leq  0 \) for all \( l \in  {S}_{\varphi }Z \) . Suppose \( l\left( {N\left( {\varphi , t}\right) }\right)  > 0 \) for some \( \varphi  \in  \partial Z \) and some \( l \in  {S}_{\varphi }Z \) . Then

\[
\frac{d}{dt}l\left( \varphi \right)  = l\left( \frac{d\varphi }{dt}\right)  = l\left( {N\left( {\varphi , t}\right) }\right)  > 0,
\]

so \( l\left( \varphi \right) \) is strictly increasing and the solution \( \varphi \left( t\right) \) of the ODE (2.3.1) cannot remain in \( Z \) .

To see the converse, first note that we may assume \( Z \) is compact. This is because we can modify the vector field \( N\left( {\varphi , t}\right) \) by multiplying a cutoff function which is everywhere nonnegative, equals one on a large ball and equals zero on the complement of a larger ball. The paths of solutions of the ODE are unchanged inside the first large ball, so we can intersect \( Z \) with the second ball to make \( Z \) convex and compact. If there were a counterexample before the modification there would still be one after as we chose the first ball large enough.

Let \( s\left( \varphi \right) \) be the distance from \( \varphi \) to \( Z \) in \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . Clearly \( s\left( \varphi \right)  = 0 \) if \( \varphi  \in  Z \) . Then

\[
s\left( \varphi \right)  = \sup \{ l\left( {\varphi  - \eta }\right)  \mid  \eta  \in  \partial Z\text{ and }l \in  {S}_{\eta }Z\} .
\]

The sup is taken over a compact subset of \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . Hence by Lemma 2.3.3

\[
\frac{d}{dt}s\left( \varphi \right)  \leq  \sup \{ l\left( {N\left( {\varphi , t}\right) }\right)  \mid  \eta  \in  \partial Z, l \in  {S}_{\eta }Z\text{ and }s\left( \varphi \right)  = l\left( {\varphi  - \eta }\right) \} .
\]

It is clear that the sup on the RHS of the above inequality can be takeen only when \( \eta \) is the unique closest point in \( Z \) to \( \varphi \) and \( l \) is the linear function of length one with gradient in the direction of \( \varphi  - \eta \) . Since \( N\left( {\varphi , t}\right) \) is Lipschitz in \( \varphi \) and continuous in \( t \) , we have

\[
\left| {N\left( {\varphi , t}\right)  - N\left( {\eta , t}\right) }\right|  \leq  C\left| {\varphi  - \eta }\right|
\]

for some constant \( C \) and all \( \varphi \) and \( \eta \) in the compact set \( Z \) .

By hypothesis (ii),

\[
l\left( {N\left( {\eta , t}\right) }\right)  \leq  0,
\]

and for the unique \( \eta \) , the closest point in \( Z \) to \( \varphi \) ,

\[
\left| {\varphi  - \eta }\right|  = s\left( \varphi \right) .
\]

Thus

\[
\frac{d}{dt}s\left( \varphi \right)  \leq  \sup \left\{  \begin{matrix} l\left( {N\left( {\eta , t}\right) }\right)  + \left| {l\left( {N\left( {\varphi , t}\right) }\right)  - l\left( {N\left( {\eta , t}\right) }\right) }\right| \; \mid  \;\eta  \in  \partial Z, \\  l \in  {S}_{\eta }Z,\;\text{ and }\;s\left( \varphi \right)  = l\left( {\varphi  - \eta }\right)  \end{matrix}\right\}
\]

\[
\leq  {Cs}\left( \varphi \right)
\]

Since \( s\left( \varphi \right)  = 0 \) to start at \( {t}_{0} \) , it follows from Lemma 2.3.2 that \( s\left( \varphi \right)  = 0 \) for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right\rbrack \) . This proves the lemma. 0

(Hamilton [65]). Let \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) ,0 \leq  t <  + \infty \) , be a noncollapsing nonsingular solution of the normalized Ricci flow on a compact three-manifold \( M \) . Then either

(i) there exist a sequence of times \( {t}_{k} \rightarrow   + \infty \) and a sequence of diffeomorphisms \( {\varphi }_{k} : M \rightarrow  M \) so that the pull-back of the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{k}\right) \) by \( {\varphi }_{k} \) converges in the \( {C}^{\infty } \) topology to a metric on \( M \) with constant sectional curvature; or

(ii) we can find a finite collection of complete noncompact hyperbolic three-manifolds \( {\mathcal{H}}_{1},\ldots ,{\mathcal{H}}_{m} \) with finite volume, and for all \( t \) beyond some time \( T <  + \infty \) we can find compact subsets \( {K}_{1},\ldots ,{K}_{m} \) of \( {\mathcal{H}}_{1},\ldots ,{\mathcal{H}}_{m} \) respectively obtained by truncating each cusp of the hyperbolic manifolds along constant mean curvature torus of small area, and diffeomorphisms \( {\varphi }_{l}\left( t\right) ,1 \leq  l \leq  m \) , of \( {K}_{l} \) into \( M \) so that as long as \( t \) sufficiently large, the pull-back of the solution metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) by \( {\varphi }_{l}\left( t\right) \) is as close as to the hyperbolic metric as we like on the compact sets \( {K}_{1},\ldots ,{K}_{m} \) ; and moreover if we call the exceptional part of \( M \) those points where they are not in the image of any \( {\varphi }_{l} \) , we can take the injectivity radii of the exceptional part at everywhere as small as we like and the boundary tori of each \( {K}_{l} \) are incompressible in the sense that each \( {\varphi }_{l} \) injects \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {\partial {K}_{l}}\right) \) into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( M\right) \) .

The rest of this section is devoted to the proof of Theorem 5.3.4. We will divide the proof into three parts.

## Part I: Subsequence Convergence

According to Lemma 5.1.1, the scalar curvature of the normalized flow evolves by the equation

(5.3.3)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}R = {\Delta R} + 2{\left| Ric\right| }^{2} - \frac{2}{3}{rR}
\]

\[
= {\Delta R} + 2\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right|  + \frac{2}{3}R\left( {R - r}\right)
\]

where \( \overset{ \circ  }{Ric} \) is the traceless part of the Ricci tensor. As before, we denote by \( {R}_{\min }\left( t\right)  = \; \mathop{\min }\limits_{{x \in  M}}R\left( {x, t}\right) \) . It then follows from the maximum principle that

(5.3.4)

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{R}_{\min } \geq  \frac{2}{3}{R}_{\min }\left( {{R}_{\min } - r}\right) ,
\]

which implies that if \( {R}_{\min } \leq  0 \) it must be nondecreasing, and if \( {R}_{\min } \geq  0 \) it cannot go negative again. We can then divide the noncollapsing solutions of the normalized Ricci flow into three cases.

Case (1): \( {R}_{\min }\left( t\right)  > 0 \) for some \( t > 0 \) ; Case (2): \( {R}_{\min }\left( t\right)  \leq  0 \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, + \infty ) \) and \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow   + \infty }}{R}_{\min }\left( t\right)  = 0 \) ; Case (3): \( {R}_{\min }\left( t\right)  \leq  0 \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, + \infty ) \) and \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow   + \infty }}{R}_{\min }\left( t\right)  < 0 \) .

Let us first consider Case (1). In this case the maximal time interval \( \lbrack 0, T) \) of the corresponding solution of the unnormalized flow is finite, since the unnormalized scalar curvature \( \widetilde{R} \) satisfies

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\widetilde{R} = \Delta \widetilde{R} + 2{\left| \widetilde{R}ic\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\geq  \Delta \widetilde{R} + \frac{2}{3}{\widetilde{R}}^{2}
\]

which implies that the curvature of the unnormalized solution blows up in finite time. Without loss of generality, we may assume that for the initial metric at \( t = 0 \) , the eigenvalues \( \widetilde{\lambda } \geq  \widetilde{\mu } \geq  \widetilde{\nu } \) of the curvature operator are bounded below by \( \widetilde{\nu } \geq   - 1 \) . It follows from Theorem 5.3.2 that the pinching estimate

\[
\widetilde{R} \geq  \left( {-\widetilde{\nu }}\right) \left\lbrack  {\log \left( {-\widetilde{\nu }}\right)  + \log \left( {1 + t}\right)  - 3}\right\rbrack
\]

holds whenever \( \widetilde{\nu } < 0 \) . This shows that when the unnormalized curvature big, the negative ones are not nearly as large as the positive ones. Note that the unnormalized curvature becomes unbounded in finite time. Thus when we rescale the unnormalized flow to the normalized flow, the scaling factor must go to infinity. In the nonsingular case the rescaled positive curvature stay finite, so the rescaled negative curvature (if any) go to zero. Hence we can take a noncollapsing limit for the nonsingular solution of the normalized flow so that it has nonnegative sectional curvature.

Since the volume of the limit is finite, it follows from a result of Calabi and Yau [112] that the limit must be compact and the limiting manifold is the original one. Then by the strong maximum principle as in the proof of Theorem 5.2.3 (i), either the limit is flat, or it is a compact metric quotient of the product of a positively curved surface \( {\sum }^{2} \) with \( \mathbb{R} \) , or it has strictly positive curvature. By the work of Schoen-Yau [110], a flat three-manifold cannot have a metric of positive scalar curvature, but our manifold does in Case (1). This rules out the possibility of a flat limit. Clearly the limit is also a nonsingular solution to the normalized Ricci flow. Note that the curvature of the surface \( {\sum }^{2} \) has a positive lower bound and is compact since it comes from the lifting of the compact limiting manifold. From Theorem 5.1.11, we see the metric of the two-dimensional factor \( {\sum }^{2} \) converges to the round two-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) in the normalized Ricci flow. Note also that the normalized factors in two-dimension and three-dimension are different. This implies that the compact quotient of the product \( {\sum }^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) cannot be nonsingular, which is also ruled out for the limit. Thus the limit must have strictly positive sectional curvature. Since the convergence takes place everywhere for the compact limit, it follows that as \( t \) large enough the original nonsingular solution has strictly positive sectional curvature. This in turn shows that the corresponding unnormalized flow has strictly positive sectional curvature after some finite time. Then in views of the proof of Theorem 5.2.1, in particular the pinching estimate in Proposition 5.2.5, the limit has constant Ricci curvature and then constant sectional curvature for three-manifolds. This finishes the proof in Case (1).

We next consider Case (2). In this case we only need to show that we can take a noncollapsing limit which has nonnegative sectional curvature. Indeed, if this is true, then as in the previous case, the limit is compact and either it is flat, or it splits as a product (or a quotient of a product) of a positively curved \( {S}^{2} \) with a circle \( {S}^{1} \) , or it has strictly positive curvature. But the assumption \( {R}_{\min }\left( t\right)  \leq  0 \) for all times \( t \geq  0 \) in this case implies the limit must be flat.

Let us consider the corresponding unnormalized flow \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) associated to the non-collapsing nonsingular solution. The pinching estimate in Theorem 5.3.2 tells us that we may assume the unnormalized flow \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) exists for all times \( 0 \leq  t <  + \infty \) , for otherwise, the scaling factor approaches infinity as in the previous case which implies the limit has nonnegative sectional curvature. The volume \( \widetilde{V}\left( t\right) \) of the unnormalized solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) now changes. We divide the discussion into three subcases.

Subcase (2.1): there is a sequence of times \( {\widetilde{t}}_{k} \rightarrow   + \infty \) such that \( \widetilde{V}\left( {\widetilde{t}}_{k}\right)  \rightarrow   + \infty \) ;

Subcase (2.2): there is a sequence of times \( {\widetilde{t}}_{k} \rightarrow   + \infty \) such that \( \widetilde{V}\left( {\widetilde{t}}_{k}\right)  \rightarrow  0 \) ;

Subcase (2.3): there exist two positive constants \( {C}_{1},{C}_{2} \) such that \( {C}_{1} \leq  \widetilde{V}\left( t\right)  \leq  {C}_{2} \) for all \( 0 \leq  t <  + \infty \) .

For Subcase (2.1), because

\[
\frac{d\widetilde{V}}{dt} =  - r\widetilde{V}
\]

we have

\[
\log \frac{\widetilde{V}\left( {\widetilde{t}}_{k}\right) }{\widetilde{V}\left( 0\right) } =  - {\int }_{0}^{{\widetilde{t}}_{k}}r\left( t\right) {dt} \rightarrow   + \infty ,\text{ as }k \rightarrow   + \infty ,
\]

which implies that there exists another sequence of times, still denoted by \( {\widetilde{t}}_{k} \) , such that \( {\widetilde{t}}_{k} \rightarrow   + \infty \) and \( r\left( {\widetilde{t}}_{k}\right)  \leq  0 \) . Let \( {t}_{k} \) be the corresponding times for the normalized flow. Thus there holds for the normalized flow

\[
r\left( {t}_{k}\right)  \rightarrow  0,\;\text{ as }\;k \rightarrow  \infty ,
\]

since \( 0 \geq  r\left( {t}_{k}\right)  \geq  {R}_{\min }\left( {t}_{k}\right)  \rightarrow  0 \) as \( k \rightarrow   + \infty \) . Then

\[
{\int }_{M}\left( {R - {R}_{\min }}\right) {d\mu }\left( {t}_{k}\right)  = \left( {r\left( {t}_{k}\right)  - {R}_{\min }\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\right) V \rightarrow  0,\;\text{ as }k \rightarrow  \infty .
\]

As we take a noncollapsing limit along the time sequence \( {t}_{k} \) , we get

\[
{\int }_{{M}^{\infty }}{Rd}{\mu }^{\infty } = 0
\]

for the limit of the normalized solutions at the new time \( t = 0 \) . But \( R \geq  0 \) for the limit because \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow   + \infty }}{R}_{\min }\left( t\right)  = 0 \) for the nonsingular solution. So \( R = 0 \) at \( t = 0 \) for the limit. Since the limit flow exists for \( - \infty  < t <  + \infty \) and the scalar curvature of the limit flow evolves by

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}R = {\Delta R} + 2{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\right| }^{2} - \frac{2}{3}{r}^{\infty }R,\;t \in  \left( {-\infty , + \infty }\right)
\]

where \( {r}^{\infty } \) is the limit of the function \( r\left( t\right) \) by translating the times \( {t}_{k} \) as the new time \( t = 0 \) . It follows from the strong maximum principle that

\[
R \equiv  0,\;\text{ on }\;{M}^{\infty } \times  \left( {-\infty , + \infty }\right) .
\]

This in turn implies, in view of the above evolution equation, that

\[
\operatorname{Ric} \equiv  0,\;\text{ on }\;{M}^{\infty } \times  \left( {-\infty , + \infty }\right) .
\]
