knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
The inclusion \( \widetilde{\mathcal{C}}\left( {\widetilde{b}}_{\max }\right)  \subset  \mathcal{C}\left( {b}_{\max }\right) \) follows immediately from the definition. We now prove the reverse inclusion \( \mathcal{C}\left( {b}_{\max }\right)  \subset  \widetilde{\mathcal{C}}\left( {\widetilde{b}}_{\max }\right) \) . For abbreviation, we put \( b = {\widetilde{b}}_{\max } \) and \( a = {\widetilde{a}}_{\max } \) . Moreover, suppose that \( S \) is an algebraic curvature tensor such that \( {\ell }_{a, b}\left( S\right)  \in  \mathcal{C}\left( {b}_{\max }\right) \) . We claim that \( S \in  \widetilde{\mathcal{E}}\left( b\right) \) . To verify this claim, we need to show that

\[
Z \mathrel{\text{ := }} {S}_{1313} + {\lambda }^{2}{S}_{1414} + {S}_{2323} + {\lambda }^{2}{S}_{2424} - {2\lambda }{S}_{1234}
\]

\[
+ \sqrt{2a}\left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right)  \geq  0
\]

for every orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) and every \( \lambda  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . To prove this, we consider the algebraic curvature tensor \( T = {\ell }_{{a}_{\max },{b}_{\max }}^{-1}\left( {{\ell }_{a, b}\left( S\right) }\right)  \in \; \mathcal{E}\left( {b}_{\max }\right) \) . Clearly, \( T \in \) PIC and \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{22} + \frac{2{\gamma }_{\max }}{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( T\right)  \geq  0 \) .

Note that \( S \) and \( T \) have the same Weyl tensor. Moreover, \( \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\left( S\right)  = \; \frac{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}_{\max }}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\left( T\right) \) and \( \operatorname{scal}\left( S\right)  = \frac{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{\max }}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\operatorname{scal}\left( T\right) \) . This gives

\[
\operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  = \frac{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}_{\max }}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\operatorname{Ric}\left( T\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{1}{n}\left( {\frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {{a}_{\max } - a}\right) }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a} - \frac{\left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {{b}_{\max } - b}\right) }{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( T\right) \text{ id }
\]

and

\[
S = T + \frac{{b}_{\max } - b}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\operatorname{Ric}\left( T\right)  \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
+ \frac{1}{n}\left( {\frac{{a}_{\max } - a}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a} - \frac{{b}_{\max } - b}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( T\right) \operatorname{id} \oslash  \operatorname{id}.
\]

Consequently,

\[
Z = {T}_{1313} + {\lambda }^{2}{T}_{1414} + {T}_{2323} + {\lambda }^{2}{T}_{2424} - {2\lambda }{T}_{1234}
\]

\[
+ \frac{{b}_{\max } - b}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\left\lbrack  {\left( {1 + {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{11} + \left( {1 + {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{22}}\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+2\operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{33} + 2{\lambda }^{2}\operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{44}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
+ \frac{4}{n}\left( {\frac{{a}_{\max } - a}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a} - \frac{{b}_{\max } - b}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}}\right) \left( {1 + {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( T\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}_{\max }}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\sqrt{2a}\left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{22}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{2}{n}\left( {\frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {{a}_{\max } - a}\right) }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a} - \frac{\left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {{b}_{\max } - b}\right) }{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}}\right) \sqrt{2a}\left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( T\right) .
\]

Using Lemma A.6, we obtain

\[
Z \geq   - \frac{1 - {\lambda }^{2}}{n - 4}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{22} - 2{T}_{1212}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{{b}_{\max } - b}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\left\lbrack  {\left( {1 + {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{11} + \left( {1 + {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{22}}\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+2\operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{33} + 2{\lambda }^{2}\operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{44}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
+ \frac{4}{n}\left( {\frac{{a}_{\max } - a}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a} - \frac{{b}_{\max } - b}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}}\right) \left( {1 + {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( T\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}_{\max }}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\sqrt{2a}\left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{22}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{2}{n}\left( {\frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {{a}_{\max } - a}\right) }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a} - \frac{\left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {{b}_{\max } - b}\right) }{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}}\right) \sqrt{2a}\left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( T\right)
\]

\[
=  : \text{ RHS. }
\]

We claim that RHS \( \geq  0 \) for all \( \lambda  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . Since RHS is a linear function of \( {\lambda }^{2} \) , it suffices to examine the endpoints of the interval:

Case 1: Suppose first that \( \lambda  = 1 \) . In this case,

\[
\mathrm{{RHS}} = 2\frac{{b}_{\max } - b}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\left\lbrack  {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{22} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{33} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{44}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
+ \frac{8}{n}\left( {\frac{{a}_{\max } - a}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a} - \frac{{b}_{\max } - b}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( T\right) .
\]

Using Lemma A.4, \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{22} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{33} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{44} \geq  0 \) . Using Lemma 4.2, we conclude that \( \mathrm{{RHS}} \geq  0 \) .

Case 2: Suppose next that \( \lambda  = 0 \) . Recall that

\[
\frac{1}{n - 4} \leq  \frac{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}_{\max }}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\sqrt{2a}\frac{{n}^{2} - {7n} + {14}}{{n}^{2} - {5n} + 4}
\]

by Lemma 4.2. Using the inequalities

\[
\operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{22} - 2{T}_{1212} \geq  0
\]

and

\[
\operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{22} + 2\operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{33}
\]

\[
= \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{33}}\right)  + \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{22} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{33}}\right)  \geq   - \frac{4{\gamma }_{\max }}{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( T\right) ,
\]

we obtain

\[
\mathrm{{RHS}} \geq   - \frac{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}_{\max }}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\sqrt{2a}\frac{{n}^{2} - {7n} + {14}}{{n}^{2} - {5n} + 4}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{22} - 2{T}_{1212}}\right)
\]

\[
- \frac{4{\gamma }_{\max }}{n}\frac{{b}_{\max } - b}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\operatorname{scal}\left( T\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{4}{n}\left( {\frac{{a}_{\max } - a}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a} - \frac{{b}_{\max } - b}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( T\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}_{\max }}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\sqrt{2a}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{22}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{2}{n}\left( {\frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {{a}_{\max } - a}\right) }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a} - \frac{\left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {{b}_{\max } - b}\right) }{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}}\right) \sqrt{2a}\operatorname{scal}\left( T\right) .
\]

Since \( T \in \) PIC, we can estimate the term \( {T}_{1212} \) in terms of \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{22} \) and \( \operatorname{scal}\left( T\right) \) :

\[
0 \leq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{3 \leq  p, q \leq  n, p \neq  q}}\left( {{T}_{1212} + {T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2q2q} + {T}_{pqpq}}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {{n}^{2} - {7n} + {14}}\right) {T}_{1212} + \left( {n - 5}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( T\right) }_{22}}\right)  + \operatorname{scal}\left( T\right) .
\]

This finally gives

\[
\mathrm{{RHS}} \geq   - \frac{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}_{\max }}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\frac{2\sqrt{2a}}{{n}^{2} - {5n} + 4}\operatorname{scal}\left( T\right)  - \frac{4{\gamma }_{\max }}{n}\frac{{b}_{\max } - b}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\operatorname{scal}\left( T\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{4}{n}\left( {\frac{{a}_{\max } - a}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a} - \frac{{b}_{\max } - b}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( T\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{2}{n}\left( {\frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {{a}_{\max } - a}\right) }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a} - \frac{\left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {{b}_{\max } - b}\right) }{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}}\right) \sqrt{2a}\operatorname{scal}\left( T\right) .
\]

Using Lemma 4.2, we obtain RHS \( \geq  0 \) . This completes the proof of Proposition 4.3.

\]

\[
Q{\left( R\right) }_{1313} + {\lambda }^{2}Q{\left( R\right) }_{1414} + {\mu }^{2}Q{\left( R\right) }_{2323} + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}Q{\left( R\right) }_{2424} - {2\lambda \mu Q}{\left( R\right) }_{1234}
\]

\[

\[

\]

\[
\left. {+\left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \left( {1 - {\mu }^{2}}\right) f\left( \text{ scal }\right) }\right)
\]

\[

\]

and the right-hand side is positive in view of our choice of \( f \) . This shows that the family of sets \( \left\{  {{\mathcal{F}}_{t} : t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) is invariant under the Hamilton ODE.

Proposition 7.18 in [5]), and consequently \( R + 2\left( {f\left( \text{ scal }\right)  + g\left( \text{ scal }\right) }\right) \) id \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC2.

\]

\[
+ \left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \left( {1 - {\mu }^{2}}\right) f\left( \text{ scal }\right)  \geq  0
\]

for \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . This ensures that \( \mathcal{K} \subset  {\mathcal{F}}_{0} \) .

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) be a complete, noncompact manifold of dimension \( n \geq  5 \) which is strictly PIC2. Suppose that \( \sum \) is a cross-sectional sphere of an \( {\varepsilon }_{0} \) -neck \( N \) in \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) . Then \( \sum \) bounds a compact domain \( \Omega \) . Moreover, there exists a diffeomorphism \( F : \Omega  \rightarrow  {B}^{n} \) and an \( {\varepsilon }_{0} \) -isometry \( f : \partial \Omega  \rightarrow  {S}^{n - 1} \) with the property that \( {\left. F\right| }_{\partial \Omega } : \partial \Omega  \rightarrow  {S}^{n - 1} \) is isotopic to \( f \) .

knowledge_statements.proof_latex: By the soul theorem (cf. [10]), \( M \) is diffeomorphic to \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . By the solution of the Schoenflies conjecture in dimension \( n \geq  5,\sum \) bounds a compact domain \( \Omega \) that is diffeomorphic to \( {B}^{n} \) . Let us choose a diffeomorphism \( F : \Omega  \rightarrow \; {B}^{n} \) , and let \( f : \partial \Omega  \rightarrow  {S}^{n - 1} \) be an \( {\varepsilon }_{0} \) -isometry. Without loss of generality, we may assume that the map \( {\left. F\right| }_{\partial \Omega } \circ  {f}^{-1} : {S}^{n - 1} \rightarrow  {S}^{n - 1} \) is orientation-preserving. We claim that the map \( {\left. F\right| }_{\partial \Omega } \circ  {f}^{-1} : {S}^{n - 1} \rightarrow  {S}^{n - 1} \) is isotopic to the identity. To prove this, let \( z \) denote the height function on the neck \( N \) , so that \( \{ z = 0\}  = \sum \) and \( \{ z \in  \lbrack  - {10},0)\}  \subset  \Omega \) . Moreover, let \( \varphi \left( z\right)  = {e}^{-\frac{1}{z}} \) for \( z \in  \left( {0,\frac{1}{10}}\right\rbrack \) . Let us define a modified metric \( \widetilde{g} \) as follows. The metric \( \widetilde{g} \) agrees with \( g \) inside \( \Omega \) . In the region \( \left\{  {z \in  \left( {0,\frac{1}{20}}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) , we change the metric conformally by \( \widetilde{g} = {e}^{-{2\varphi }}g \) . In the region \( \left\{  {z \in  \left( {\frac{1}{20},\frac{1}{10}}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) , we define \( \widetilde{g} = {e}^{-{2\varphi }}\left( {\chi \left( z\right) g + \left( {1 - \chi \left( z\right) }\right) \bar{g}}\right) \) , where \( \bar{g} \) denotes the standard metric on the cylinder and \( \chi  : \left( {\frac{1}{20},\frac{1}{10}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) is a smooth cutoff function satisfying \( \chi \left( z\right)  = 1 \) for \( z \in  \left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{20},\frac{1}{18}}\right\rbrack \) and \( \chi \left( z\right)  = 0 \) for \( z \in  \left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{12},\frac{1}{10}}\right\rbrack \) . Since the original metric \( g \) is strictly PIC2, the modified metric \( \widetilde{g} \) will be strictly PIC2 in the region \( \left\{  {z \in  \left( {0,\frac{1}{10}}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) . Moreover, the surgically modified metric \( \widetilde{g} \) is rotationally symmetric for \( z \in  \left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{12},\frac{1}{10}}\right\rbrack \) . Consequently, we can extend \( \widetilde{g} \) by gluing in a rotationally symmetric cap. This can be done in such a way that the glued metric is strictly PIC2. To summarize, we obtain a closed manifold that is obtained by gluing two balls, and that admits a metric that is strictly PIC2. If the map \( {\left. F\right| }_{\partial \Omega } \circ  {f}^{-1} \) is not isotopic to the identity, then this glued manifold is an exotic sphere, that contradicts the fact that exotic spheres do not admit metrics that are strictly PIC2 (cf. [8]).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  (0, T\rbrack \) , be a complete solution to the Ricci flow (possibly with unbounded curvature). Moreover, we assume that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is weakly PIC2 and strictly PIC. Suppose that there exists a point \( \left( {{p}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) in space-time with the property that the curvature tensor at \( \left( {{p}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) lies on the boundary of the PIC2 cone. Then, for each \( t \leq  {t}_{0} \) , the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) splits off a line.

knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
Suppose that the assertion is false. Then there exists a time \( \tau  \in \; \left( {0,{t}_{0}}\right) \) with the property that the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) does not split off a line. Since \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC, we conclude that \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is locally irreducible. In view of Berger's holonomy classification theorem, there are four possible cases:

Case 1: Suppose first that \( {\operatorname{Hol}}^{0}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = {SO}\left( n\right) \) . If we fix an arbitrary pair of real numbers \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) , then Theorem 9.13 in [5] implies that the set of all orthonormal four-frames \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) satisfying

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {\mu }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda \mu }{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  = 0
\]

is invariant under parallel transport. Since \( {\operatorname{Hol}}^{0}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = {SO}\left( n\right) \) , we conclude that

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {\mu }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda \mu }{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  > 0
\]

for all orthonormal four-frames \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) and all \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . In other words, the curvature tensor of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) lies in the interior of the PIC2 cone.

Let \( \Omega \) be a bounded open neighborhood of the point \( {p}_{0} \) with smooth boundary. Let us choose a smooth function \( f : \bar{\Omega } \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) with the property that \( f > 0 \) in \( \Omega , f = 0 \) on \( \partial \Omega \) , and \( {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) } - \frac{1}{2}f \) id \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC2. Let \( F \) : \( \bar{\Omega } \times  \left\lbrack  {\tau ,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) denote the solution of the linear heat equation with respect to the evolving metric \( g\left( t\right) \) with initial data \( F\left( {\cdot ,\tau }\right)  = f \) and Dirichlet boundary condition \( F = 0 \) on \( \partial \Omega  \times  \left\lbrack  {\tau ,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . Let \( S \mathrel{\text{ := }} {R}_{g\left( t\right) } - \frac{1}{2}F\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) id \( \oslash \) id. Then \( {D}_{t}S = {\Delta S} + Q\left( S\right)  + {2F}\operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{id} + \left( {n - 1}\right) {F}^{2}\operatorname{id} \oslash  \operatorname{id} \) . Using the maximum principle, we conclude that \( {R}_{g\left( t\right) } - \frac{1}{2}F\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) id \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC2 at each point in \( \Omega  \times  \left\lbrack  {\tau ,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . Since \( F\left( {{p}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  > 0 \) , the curvature tensor at \( \left( {{p}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) lies in the interior of the PIC2 cone, contrary to our assumption.

Case 2: Suppose that \( n = {2m} \) and \( {\operatorname{Hol}}^{0}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = U\left( m\right) \) . In this case, the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is a Kähler manifold. This is impossible since \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC.

Case 3: Suppose next that \( n = {4m} \geq  8 \) and \( {\operatorname{Hol}}^{0}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = \operatorname{Sp}\left( m\right) \) . \( \mathrm{{Sp}}\left( 1\right) \) . In this case, the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is a quaternionic Kähler manifold. In particular, \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is an Einstein manifold. Since \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC, we conclude that the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is a round sphere (cf. [4]). This is impossible.

Case 4: Suppose finally that \( {\operatorname{Hol}}^{0}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  \neq  {SO}\left( n\right) \) and \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is locally symmetric. In this case, \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is an Einstein manifold, for otherwise the eigenspaces of the Ricci tensor give a splitting of the tangent bundle into parallel subbundles, which is impossible since \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is locally irreducible. Since \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC, it follows that the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is a round sphere (cf. [4]). This contradicts the fact that \( {\operatorname{Hol}}^{0}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  \neq  {SO}\left( n\right) \) . This completes the proof of Theorem 6.6.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) , is a complete ancient solution to the Ricci flow that is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales, is weakly PIC2, and satisfies \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \varnothing \) id \( \in \) PIC for some uniform constant \( \theta  > 0 \) . Moreover, suppose that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies the Harnack inequality

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\operatorname{scal} + 2\langle \nabla \operatorname{scal}, v\rangle  + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {v, v}\right)  \geq  0
\]

for every tangent vector \( v \) . Then \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) has bounded curvature.

knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
Since \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies the Harnack inequality, it suffices to show that \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) has bounded curvature. The proof is by contradiction. Suppose that \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) has unbounded curvature.

By the strict maximum principle, we can find a real number \( \delta  > 0 \) with the property that the scalar curvature \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is strictly positive for \( t \in  ( - \delta ,0\rbrack \) .

Consequently, \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC for \( t \in  ( - \delta ,0\rbrack \) . We distinguish two cases:

Case 1: Suppose first that \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC2. In this case, \( M \) is diffeomorphic to \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) by the soul theorem (cf. [10]). By a standard point-picking argument, there exists a sequence of points \( {x}_{j} \in  M \) such that \( {Q}_{j} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \; \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right)  \geq  {j}^{4} \) and

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j},{2j}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  4{Q}_{j}.
\]

Since \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies the Harnack inequality, we obtain

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j},{2j}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-4{j}^{2}{Q}_{j}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack  }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  4{Q}_{j}.
\]

Using Shi's interior derivative estimate, we obtain bounds for all the derivatives of curvature on \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j}, j{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-{j}^{2}{Q}_{j}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) . We now dilate the flow \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) around the point \( \left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) \) by the factor \( {Q}_{j} \) . Using the noncollapsing assumption and the curvature derivative estimates, we conclude that, after passing to a subsequence, the rescaled flows converge in the Cheeger-Gromov sense to a smooth nonflat ancient solution \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) . The limit \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is complete, has bounded curvature, is weakly PIC2, and satisfies \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} \in \) PIC. By Proposition 6.8, the manifold \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) splits off a line. By Corollary 6.7, universal cover of \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a family of shrinking cylinders \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) . Therefore, \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a quotient \( \left( {{S}^{n - 1}/\Gamma }\right)  \times  \mathbb{R} \) . If \( \Gamma \) is nontrivial, then a result of Hamilton implies that \( M \) contains a nontrivial incompressible \( \left( {n - 1}\right) \) -dimensional space form \( {S}^{n - 1}/\Gamma \) (cf. [6, Th. A.2]), but this is impossible since \( M \) is diffeomorphic to \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . Thus, \( \Gamma \) is trivial, and \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a standard cylinder \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) . Consequently, \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) contains a sequence of necks with radii converging to 0 . This contradicts Proposition 6.9.

Case 2: Suppose finally that \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is not strictly PIC2. By Proposition 6.6, the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a product \( \left( {X,{g}_{X}\left( t\right) }\right)  \times  \mathbb{R} \) for each \( t \in  ( - \delta ,0\rbrack \) . Clearly, \( \left( {X,{g}_{X}\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  ( - \delta ,0\rbrack \) , is a complete solution to the Ricci flow of dimension \( n - 1 \) , which is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales, weakly PIC2, and uniformly PIC1. By assumption, \( \left( {X,{g}_{X}\left( 0\right) }\right) \) has unbounded curvature. Using a point-picking lemma, we can construct a sequence of points \( {x}_{j} \in  X \) such that \( {Q}_{j} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right)  \geq  {j}^{4} \) and

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{{g}_{X}\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j},{2j}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  4{Q}_{j}.
\]

As in Case 1, the Harnack inequality and Shi's interior derivative estimate give bounds for all the derivatives of curvature on \( {B}_{{g}_{X}\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j}, j{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-{j}^{2}{Q}_{j}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) . We now dilate the manifold \( \left( {X,{g}_{X}\left( 0\right) }\right) \) around the point \( {x}_{j} \) by the factor \( {Q}_{j} \) . Passing to the limit as \( j \rightarrow  \infty \) , we obtain a smooth nonflat limit that is uniformly PIC1 and that must split off a line by Proposition 6.8. This is a contradiction.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: (cf. G. Perelman [33], Chen-Zhu [12]). Fix \( \theta  > 0 \) . We can find a constant \( {\kappa }_{0} = {\kappa }_{0}\left( {n,\theta }\right) \) such that the following holds: Suppose that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is an ancient \( \kappa \) -solution for some \( \kappa  > 0 \) , which in addition satisfies \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC. Then either \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is \( {\kappa }_{0} \) -noncollapsed for all \( t \) ; or \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a metric quotient of the round sphere \( {S}^{n} \) ; or \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a noncompact metric quotient of the standard cylinder \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) .

If \( M \) is noncompact, the assertion follows from Theorem 6.18. Hence, we may assume that \( M \) is compact. Moreover, we may assume that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is not a metric quotient of the round sphere \( {S}^{n} \) . The noncollapsing assumption implies that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) cannot be a compact quotient of a standard cylinder. By Corollary 6.7, \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC2.

Consider a sequence of times \( {t}_{j} \rightarrow   - \infty \) and a sequence of points \( {q}_{j} \in  M \) such that \( \ell \left( {{q}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right)  \leq  n \) , where \( \ell \) denotes the reduced distance. By Perelman’s work, \( \ell \left( {x,{t}_{j}}\right)  + \left( {-{t}_{j}}\right) R\left( {x,{t}_{j}}\right)  \leq  C\left( n\right) \) for all \( x \in  {B}_{g\left( {t}_{j}\right) }\left( {{q}_{j},{\left( -{t}_{j}\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \) . If we dilate the flow \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) around the point \( \left( {{q}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \) by the factor \( {\left( -{t}_{j}\right) }^{-1} \) , then the rescaled flows converge to a complete ancient solution \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) (cf. [33, §11.2]). Perelman proved that the limit \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a nonflat shrinking gradient Ricci soliton. Clearly, \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed, weakly PIC2, and satisfies \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC. Moreover, since the Harnack inequality holds on \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) , it holds on the limit \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) . By Proposition 6.11, \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) has bounded curvature. We distinguish two cases:

Case 1: We first consider the case that \( \bar{M} \) is compact. A shrinking soliton \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) cannot be isometric to a compact quotient of a standard cylinder. By

Corollary 6.7, \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC2. Since \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a shrinking soliton, results in [8] imply that \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) must be isometric to a metric quotient of the round sphere \( {S}^{n} \) . Consequently, the original ancient solution \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a metric quotient of \( {S}^{n} \) , contrary to our assumption.

Case 2: Suppose next that \( \bar{M} \) is noncompact. In view of Theorem 6.18, there are two possibilities: either \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) is \( {\kappa }_{0} \) -noncollapsed for some universal constant \( {\kappa }_{0} = {\kappa }_{0}\left( {n,\theta }\right) \) , or else \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a noncompact quotient of the standard cylinder. The second case can be divided into two subcases:

- If the dimension \( n \) is odd and \( \bar{M} \) is a noncompact quotient \( \left( {{S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R}}\right) /\Gamma \) , then there are only finitely many possibilities for the group \( \Gamma \) , and the resulting quotients are all noncollapsed with a universal constant.

- If the dimension \( n \) is even and \( \bar{M} \) is a noncompact quotient \( \left( {{S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R}}\right) /\Gamma \) , then the center slice \( \left( {{S}^{n - 1}\times \{ 0\} }\right) /\Gamma \) is incompressible in \( M \) by Theorem A. 1 in [6]. Moreover, since \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC2, the fundamental group of \( M \) has order at most 2 by Synge’s theorem. Hence, there are only finitely many possibilities for the group \( \Gamma \) , and the resulting quotients \( \left( {{S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R}}\right) /\Gamma \) are noncollapsed with a universal constant.

To summarize, we have shown that the asymptotic shrinking soliton \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) is noncollapsed with a universal constant that depends only on \( n \) and \( \theta \) . This implies \( \mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}{\left( -{t}_{j}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( {t}_{j}\right) }\left( {{B}_{g\left( {t}_{j}\right) }\left( {{q}_{j},{\left( -{t}_{j}\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{C\left( {n,\theta }\right) } \) . Hence, if \( V\left( t\right)  = \; {\int }_{M}{\left( -t\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-\ell \left( {\cdot , t}\right) }d{\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( t\right) } \) denotes the reduced volume, then \( \mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}V\left( {t}_{j}\right)  \geq \; \frac{1}{C\left( {n,\theta }\right) } \) . Perelman’s monotonicity formula gives \( V\left( t\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{C\left( {n,\theta }\right) } \) . Thus, \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is noncollapsed with a universal constant that depends only on \( n \) and \( \theta \) .

\left| {{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {30}\bar{Q},
\]

for all \( x \in  {B}_{t}\left( {\bar{x},\frac{1}{10}{\eta }^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\widetilde{t} - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-1},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) (or \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) ) and all sufficiently large \( \alpha \) and \( \beta \) . Observe that Lemma 3.4.1 (ii) is applicable for \( {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},\bar{x}}\right) \) with \( t \in \; \left\lbrack  {\widetilde{t} - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-1},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) (or \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) ) since any minimal geodesic, with respect to the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) , connecting \( {x}_{0} \) and \( \bar{x} \) lies in the region unaffected by surgery; otherwise the geodesic is not minimal. After having obtained the above curvature estimate, we can argue as deriving (7.2.2) and (7.2.3) in the proof of Theorem 7.2.1 to conclude that any point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) , with \( \widetilde{t} - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-1} \leq  t \leq  \bar{t} \) (or \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) ) and \( {d}_{t}\left( {x,\bar{x}}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{10}{K}_{1}^{\frac{1}{2}}{\bar{Q}}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) , satisfies

\[
{d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  \leq  {d}_{\bar{t}}\left( {\bar{x},{x}_{0}}\right)  + \frac{1}{2}{K}_{1}^{\frac{1}{2}}{\bar{Q}}^{-\frac{1}{2}},
\]

for all sufficiently large \( \alpha \) and \( \beta \) . Then by combining with the choice of the points \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) , we prove \( {t}^{\prime } = \bar{t} - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-1} \) (i.e., the canonical neighborhood statement holds for any point \( \left( {y, t}\right) \) in the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t},\frac{1}{10}{K}_{1}^{\frac{1}{2}}{\bar{Q}}^{-\frac{1}{2}}, - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-1}}\right) \) with \( R\left( {y, t}\right)  \geq  4\bar{Q} \) ) for all sufficiently large \( \alpha \) and then sufficiently large \( \beta \) .

Now it follows from the gradient estimates in the canonical neighborhood assumption that the scalar curvatures of the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) satisfy

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {40}
\]

for those \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  P\left( {\bar{x},0,\frac{1}{10}{\eta }^{-1}, - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}}\right)  \triangleq  \left\{  {\left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \mid  {x}^{\prime } \in  {\widetilde{B}}_{{t}^{\prime }}\left( {\bar{x},\frac{1}{10}{\eta }^{-1}}\right) ,{t}^{\prime } \in  }\right. \; \left. \left\lbrack  {-\frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack  \right\} \) , for which the rescaled solution is defined. (Here \( {\widetilde{B}}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) denotes the geodesic ball in the rescaled solution at time \( {t}^{\prime } \) ). Note again that \( R\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  \leq  \widetilde{r}{\left( \bar{t}\right) }^{-2} \) and recall from our designed surgery procedure that if there is a cutoff surgery at a point \( x \) at a time \( t \) , the scalar curvature at \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) is at least \( {\left( {\bar{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta }\right) }^{-2}\widetilde{r}{\left( t\right) }^{-2} \) . Then for each fixed sufficiently large \( \alpha \) , for \( \beta \) large enough, the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) is defined on the whole parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {\bar{x},0,\frac{1}{10}{\eta }^{-1}, - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}}\right) \) . More generally, for arbitrarily fixed \( 0 < \widetilde{K} <  + \infty \) , there is a positive integer \( {\alpha }_{0} \) so that for each \( \alpha  \geq  {\alpha }_{0} \) we can

find \( {\beta }_{0} > 0 \) (depending on \( \alpha \) ) such that if \( \beta  \geq  {\beta }_{0} \) and \( \left( {y,0}\right) \) is a point on the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) with \( \widetilde{R}\left( {y,0}\right)  \leq  \widetilde{K} \) and \( {\widetilde{d}}_{0}\left( {y,\bar{x}}\right)  \leq  \widetilde{K} \) , we have estimate

(7.5.14)

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {40}\widetilde{K}
\]

for \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  P\left( {y,0,\frac{1}{10}{\eta }^{-1}{\widetilde{K}}^{-\frac{1}{2}}, - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\widetilde{K}}^{-1}}\right)  \triangleq  \left\{  {\left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \mid  {x}^{\prime } \in  {\widetilde{B}}_{{t}^{\prime }}\left( {y,}\right) }\right. \; \left. {\left. {\frac{1}{10}{\eta }^{-1}{\widetilde{K}}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right\rbrack  ,{t}^{\prime } \in  \left\lbrack  {-\frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\widetilde{K}}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) . In particular, the rescaled solution is defined on the whole parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {y,0,\frac{1}{10}{\eta }^{-1}{\widetilde{K}}^{-\frac{1}{2}}, - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\widetilde{K}}^{-1}}\right) \) .

Next, we want to show the curvature of the rescaled solutions at the new times zero (after shifting) stay uniformly bounded at bounded distances from \( \bar{x} \) for some subsequences of \( \alpha \) and \( \beta \) . Let \( {\alpha }_{m},{\beta }_{m} \rightarrow   + \infty \) be chosen so that the estimate (7.5.14) holds with \( \widetilde{K} = m \) . For all \( \rho  \geq  0 \) , set

\[
M\left( \rho \right)  = \sup \left\{  {\widetilde{R}\left( {x,0}\right)  \mid  m \geq  1,{d}_{0}\left( {x,\bar{x}}\right)  \leq  \rho \text{ in the rescaled solutions }{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}}}\right\}
\]

and

\[
{\rho }_{0} = \sup \{ \rho  \geq  0 \mid  M\left( \rho \right)  <  + \infty \} .
\]

Clearly the estimate (7.5.14) yields \( {\rho }_{0} > 0 \) . As we consider the unshifted time \( \bar{t} \) , by combining with the assumption that \( {t}_{0} > 2{r}_{0}^{2} \) , we have

(7.5.15)

\[
\bar{t}R\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  \geq  \frac{{t}_{0}}{2}R\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  {r}_{0}^{2}\left( {{K}_{1}{r}_{0}^{-2}}\right)
\]

\[
= {K}_{1} \rightarrow   + \infty \text{ . }
\]

It then follows from the pinching assumption that we only need to show \( {\rho }_{0} =  + \infty \) . As before, we argue by contradiction. Suppose we have a sequence of points \( {y}_{m} \) in the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}} \) with \( {\widetilde{d}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x},{y}_{m}}\right)  \rightarrow  {\rho }_{0} <  + \infty \) and \( \widetilde{R}\left( {{y}_{m},0}\right)  \rightarrow   + \infty \) . Denote by \( {\gamma }_{m} \) a minimizing geodesic segment from \( \bar{x} \) to \( {y}_{m} \) and denote by \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x},{\rho }_{0}}\right) \) the open geodesic balls centered at \( \bar{x} \) of radius \( {\rho }_{0} \) of the rescaled solutions. By applying the assertion in statement (i), we have uniform \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing at the points \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) . By combining with the local curvature estimate (7.5.14) and Hamilton's compactness theorem, we can assume that, after passing to a subsequence, the marked sequence \( \left( {{\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x},{\rho }_{0}}\right) ,{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}},\bar{x}}\right) \) converges in the \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) topology to a marked (noncomplete) manifold \( \left( {{B}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty },{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) and the geodesic segments \( {\gamma }_{m} \) converge to a geodesic segment (missing an endpoint) \( {\gamma }_{\infty } \subset  {B}_{\infty } \) emanating from \( {x}_{\infty } \) . Moreover, by the pinching assumption and the estimate (7.5.15), the limit has nonnegative sectional curvature.

Then exactly as before, we consider the tubular neighborhood along \( {\gamma }_{\infty } \)

\[
V = \mathop{\bigcup }\limits_{{{q}_{0} \in  {\gamma }_{\infty }}}{B}_{\infty }\left( {{q}_{0},{4\pi }{\left( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {q}_{0}\right) \right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)
\]

and the completion \( {\bar{B}}_{\infty } \) of \( \left( {{B}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty }}\right) \) with \( {y}_{\infty } \in  {\bar{B}}_{\infty } \) the limit point of \( {\gamma }_{\infty } \) . As before, by the choice of the points \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) , we know that the limiting metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty } \) is cylindrical at any point \( {q}_{0} \in  {\gamma }_{\infty } \) which is sufficiently close to \( {y}_{\infty } \) . Then by the same reason as before the metric space \( \bar{V} = V \cup  \left\{  {y}_{\infty }\right\} \) has nonnegative curvature in Alexandrov sense, and we have a three-dimensional nonflat tangent cone \( {C}_{{y}_{\infty }}\bar{V} \) at \( {y}_{\infty } \) . Pick \( z \in  {C}_{{y}_{\infty }}\bar{V} \) with distance one from the vertex and it is nonflat around \( z \) . By definition \( B\left( {z,\frac{1}{2}}\right) \left( { \subset  {C}_{{y}_{\infty }}\bar{V}}\right) \) is the Gromov-Hausdoff convergent limit of the scalings of a sequence of balls \( {B}_{\infty }\left( {{z}_{k},{\sigma }_{k}}\right) \left( { \subset  \left( {V,{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty }}\right) }\right) \) with \( {\sigma }_{k} \rightarrow  0 \) . Since the estimate (7.5.14) survives on \( \left( {V,{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty }}\right) \) for all \( \widetilde{K} <  + \infty \) , we know that this convergence is actually in the \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) topology and over some time interval. Since the limit \( B\left( {z,\frac{1}{2}}\right) \left( { \subset  {C}_{{y}_{\infty }}\bar{V}}\right) \) is a piece of a nonnegatively curved nonflat metric cone, we get a contradiction with Hamilton's strong maximum Principle (Theorem 2.2.1) as before. Hence we have proved that a subsequence of the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}} \) has uniformly bounded curvatures at bounded distance from \( \bar{x} \) at the new times zero.

Further, by the uniform \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing at the points \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) and the estimate (7.5.14) again, we can take a \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) limit \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty },{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) , defined on a space-time subset which contains the time slice \( \{ t = 0\} \) and is relatively open in \( {M}_{\infty } \times  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) , for the subsequence of the rescaled solutions. The limit is a smooth solution to the Ricci flow, and is complete at \( t = 0 \) , as well as has nonnegative sectional curvature by the pinching assumption and the estimate (7.5.15). Thus by repeating the same argument as in the Step 4 of the proof Proposition 7.4.1, we conclude that the curvature of the limit at \( t = 0 \) is bounded.

Finally we try to extend the limit backwards in time to get an ancient \( \kappa \) -solution. Since the curvature of the limit is bounded at \( t = 0 \) , it follows from the estimate (7.5.14) that the limit is a smooth solution to the Ricci flow defined at least on a backward time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-a,0}\right\rbrack \) for some positive constant \( a \) . Let \( \left( {{t}_{\infty },0}\right\rbrack \) be the maximal time interval over which we can extract a smooth limiting solution. It suffices to show \( {t}_{\infty } =  - \infty \) . If \( {t}_{\infty } >  - \infty \) , there are only two possibilities: either there exist surgeries in finite distance around the time \( {t}_{\infty } \) or the curvature of the limiting solution becomes unbounded as \( t \searrow  {t}_{\infty } \) .

Let \( c > 0 \) be a positive constant much smaller than \( \frac{1}{100}{\eta }^{-1} \) . Note again that the infimum of the scalar curvature is nondecreasing in time. Then we can find some point \( {y}_{\infty } \in  {M}_{\infty } \) and some time \( t = {t}_{\infty } + \theta \) with \( 0 < \theta  < \frac{c}{3} \) such that \( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {{y}_{\infty },{t}_{\infty } + \theta }\right)  \leq  2 \) .

Consider the (unrescaled) scalar curvature \( R \) of \( {g}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) at the point \( \bar{x} \) over the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {\bar{t} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + \frac{\theta }{2}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) . Since the scalar curvature \( {R}_{\infty } \) of the limit on \( {M}_{\infty } \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{\infty } + \frac{\theta }{3},0}\right\rbrack \) is uniformly bounded by some positive constant \( C \) , we have the curvature estimate

\[
R\left( {\bar{x}, t}\right)  \leq  {2C}\bar{Q}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + \frac{\theta }{2}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) and all sufficiently large \( m \) . For each fixed \( m \) and \( {\alpha }_{m} \) , we may require the chosen \( {\beta }_{m} \) to satisfy

\[
{\left( {\bar{\delta }}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}}\right) }^{-2}{\left( \widetilde{r}\left( \frac{{t}_{0}^{{\alpha }_{m}}}{2}\right) \right) }^{-2} \geq  m\widetilde{r}{\left( {t}_{0}^{{\alpha }_{m}}\right) }^{-2} \geq  m\bar{Q}.
\]

When \( m \) is large enough, we observe again that Lemma 3.4.1 (ii) is applicable for \( {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},\bar{x}}\right) \) with \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + \frac{\theta }{2}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) . Then by repeating the argument as in the derivation of (7.2.1),(7.2.2) and (7.2.3), we deduce that for all sufficiently large \( m \) , the canonical neighborhood statement holds for any \( \left( {y, t}\right) \) in the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t},\frac{1}{10}{K}_{1}^{\frac{1}{2}}{\bar{Q}}^{-\frac{1}{2}},\left( {{t}_{\infty } + \frac{\theta }{2}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1}}\right) . \)

Let \( \left( {{y}_{m},\bar{t} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + {\theta }_{m}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1}}\right) \) be a sequence of associated points and times in the (unrescaled) solutions \( {g}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) so that after rescaling, the sequence converges to \( \left( {{y}_{\infty },{t}_{\infty } + \theta }\right) \) in the limit. Clearly \( \frac{\theta }{2} \leq  {\theta }_{m} \leq  {2\theta } \) for all sufficiently large \( m \) . Then by the argument as in the derivation of (7.5.13), we know that for all sufficiently large \( m \) , the solution \( {g}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) at \( {y}_{m} \) is defined on the whole time interval \( \left\lbrack  {\bar{t} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + {\theta }_{m} - }\right. }\right. \; \left. {\left. {\frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1},\bar{t} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + {\theta }_{m}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1}}\right\rbrack \) and satisfies the curvature estimate

\[
R\left( {{y}_{m}, t}\right)  \leq  8\bar{Q}
\]

there; moreover the canonical neighborhood statement holds for any \( \left( {y, t}\right) \) with \( R\left( {y, t}\right)  \geq  4\bar{Q} \) in the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {{y}_{m},\bar{t},\frac{1}{10}{K}_{1}^{\frac{1}{2}}{\bar{Q}}^{-\frac{1}{2}},\left( {{t}_{\infty } - \frac{c}{3}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1}}\right) \) .

We now consider the rescaled sequence \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) with the marked points replaced by \( {y}_{m} \) and the times replaced by \( {s}_{m} \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } - \frac{c}{4}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1},\bar{t} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + \frac{c}{4}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1}}\right\rbrack \) . As before the Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality implies the rescaling limit around \( \left( {{y}_{m},{s}_{m}}\right) \) agrees with the original one. Then the arguments in previous paragraphs imply the limit is well-defined and smooth on a space-time open neighborhood of the maximal time slice \( \left\{  {t = {t}_{\infty }}\right\} \) . Particularly this excludes the possibility of existing surgeries in finite distance around the time \( {t}_{\infty } \) . Moreover, the limit at \( t = {t}_{\infty } \) also has bounded curvature. By using the gradient estimates in the canonical neighborhood assumption on the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {{y}_{m},\bar{t},\frac{1}{10}{K}_{1}^{\frac{1}{2}}{\bar{Q}}^{-\frac{1}{2}},\left( {{t}_{\infty } - \frac{c}{3}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1}}\right) \) , we see that the second possibility is also impossible. Hence we have proved a subsequence of the rescaled solutions converges to an ancient \( \kappa \) -solution.

Therefore we have proved the canonical neighborhood statement (ii).

(iii) This is analogous to Theorem 7.2.1. We also argue by contradiction. Suppose for some \( A <  + \infty \) and sequences of positive numbers \( {K}_{2}^{\alpha } \rightarrow   + \infty ,{\bar{r}}^{\alpha } \rightarrow  0 \) there exists a sequence of times \( {t}_{0}^{\alpha } \) such that for any sequences \( {\bar{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } > 0 \) with \( {\bar{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } \rightarrow  0 \) for fixed \( \alpha \) , we have sequences of solutions \( {g}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) to the Ricci flow with surgery and sequences of points \( {x}_{0}^{\alpha \beta } \) , of positive constants \( {r}_{0}^{\alpha \beta } \) with \( {r}_{0}^{\alpha \beta } \leq  {\bar{r}}^{\alpha }\sqrt{{t}_{0}^{\alpha }} \) which satisfy the assumptions, but for all \( \alpha ,\beta \) there hold

(7.5.16)

\[
R\left( {{x}^{\alpha \beta },{t}_{0}^{\alpha }}\right)  > {K}_{2}^{\alpha }{\left( {r}_{0}^{\alpha \beta }\right) }^{-2}\text{ , for some }{x}^{\alpha \beta } \in  {B}_{{t}_{0}^{\alpha }}\left( {{x}_{0}^{\alpha \beta }, A{r}_{0}^{\alpha \beta }}\right) .
\]

We may assume that \( {\bar{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } \leq  {\bar{\delta }}_{4A}\left( {t}_{0}^{\alpha }\right) \) for all \( \alpha ,\beta \) , where \( {\bar{\delta }}_{4A}\left( {t}_{0}^{\alpha }\right) \) is chosen so that the statements (i) and (ii) hold on \( {B}_{{t}_{0}^{\alpha }}\left( {{x}_{0}^{\alpha \beta },{4A}{r}_{0}^{\alpha \beta }}\right) \) . Let \( {\widehat{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) be the rescaled solutions of \( {g}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) around the origins \( {x}_{0}^{\alpha \beta } \) with factor \( {\left( {r}_{0}^{\alpha \beta }\right) }^{-2} \) and shift the times \( {t}_{0}^{\alpha } \) to zero. Then by applying the statement (ii), we know that the regions, where the scalar curvature of the rescaled solutions \( {\widehat{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) is at least \( {K}_{1}\left( { = {K}_{1}\left( {4A}\right) }\right) \) , are canonical neighborhood regions. Note that canonical \( \varepsilon \) -neck neighborhoods are strong. Also note that the pinching assumption and the assertion

\[
{t}_{0}^{\alpha }{\left( {r}_{0}^{\alpha \beta }\right) }^{-2} \geq  {\left( {\bar{r}}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-2} \rightarrow   + \infty ,\text{ as }\alpha  \rightarrow   + \infty ,
\]

imply that any subsequent limit of the rescaled solutions \( {\widehat{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) must have nonnegative sectional curvature. Thus by the above argument in the proof of the statement (ii) (or the argument in Step 2 of the proof of Theorem 7.1.1), we conclude that there exist subsequences \( \alpha  = {\alpha }_{m},\beta  = {\beta }_{m} \) such that the curvatures of the rescaled solutions \( {\widehat{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}} \) stay uniformly bounded at distances from the origins \( {x}_{0}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}} \) not exceeding \( {2A} \) . This contradicts (7.5.16) for \( m \) sufficiently large. This proves the statements (iii).

Clearly for fixed \( A \) , after defining the \( {\bar{\delta }}_{A}\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) for each \( {t}_{0} \) , one can adjust the \( {\bar{\delta }}_{A}\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) so that it is nonincreasing in \( {t}_{0} \) .

Therefore we have completed the proof of the theorem.

From now on we redefine the function \( \widetilde{\delta }\left( t\right) \) so that it is also less than \( {\bar{\delta }}_{2\left( {t + 1}\right) }\left( {2t}\right) \) and then the above theorem always holds for \( A \in  \left\lbrack  {1,2\left( {{t}_{0} + 1}\right) }\right\rbrack \) . Particularly, we still

have

\[
\widetilde{\delta }\left( t\right)  \leq  \bar{\delta }\left( t\right)  = \min \left\{  {\frac{1}{2{e}^{2}\log \left( {1 + t}\right) },{\delta }_{0}}\right\}  ,
\]

which tends to zero as \( t \rightarrow   + \infty \) . We may also require that \( \widetilde{r}\left( t\right) \) tends to zero as \( t \rightarrow   + \infty \) .

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
(Existence of a generalized pinching set). Let

\[
{C}_{\clubsuit }{\left( s\right) }_{s \in  \lbrack 0,1)} \subset  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right)
\]

be a continuous family of closed convex \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant cones of maximum dimension, such that \( {C}_{4}\left( s\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) is contained in the half-space of curvature operators with positive scalar curvature for all \( s \in  \lbrack 0,1) \) . Suppose that for \( \mathbf{R} \in  \partial {C}_{ \bullet  }\left( s\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) the vector field \( Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone of \( {C}_{ \bullet  }\left( s\right) \) at \( \mathbf{R} \) for all \( s \in  \left( {0,1}\right) \) . Then for any \( \varepsilon  \in  \left( {0,1}\right) \) and \( {h}_{0} \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) there exists a closed convex \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant subset \( F \subset \; {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) with the following properties:

(1) \( F \) is preserved by the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}\mathbf{R} = {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } \) ;

(2) \( {C}_{ \bullet  }\left( \varepsilon \right)  \cap  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \leq  {h}_{0}}\right\}   \subset  F \subset  {C}_{ \bullet  }\left( \varepsilon \right) \) ;

(3) \( \overline{F \smallsetminus  {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( s\right) } \) is compact (i.e., bounded) for all \( s \in  \lbrack \varepsilon ,1) \) .

knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
Fix any \( \varepsilon  \in  \left( {0,1}\right) \) and \( {h}_{0} \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) . Define the set \( F \) to be the intersection of all closed convex \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant subsets of \( {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) satisfying properties (1) and (2) in the statement of Theorem 11.64. We want to show that \( F \) is the desired generalized pinching set. Since \( {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( \varepsilon \right) \) is such a set, \( F \) is a well-defined closed convex \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant subset contained in \( {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( \varepsilon \right) \) .

(I) Suppose \( {\mathbf{R}}_{0} \in  F \) and \( \mathbf{R}\left( t\right) \) is a solution of the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}\mathbf{R} = Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) with \( \mathbf{R}\left( 0\right)  = {\mathbf{R}}_{0} \) . Then for any closed convex \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant subset \( G \) of \( {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) satisfying properties (1) and (2), \( {}^{29} \) we have \( \mathbf{R}\left( t\right)  \in  G \) . Hence, by definition, \( \mathbf{R}\left( t\right)  \in  F \) . Thus property (1) holds for \( F \) .

(II) It is also clear that property (2) holds for \( F \) , i.e.,

\[
{C}_{\text{ ♣ }}\left( \varepsilon \right)  \cap  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \leq  {h}_{0}}\right\}   \subset  F.
\]

(III) It remains to prove property (3). Suppose, with the goal of obtaining a contradiction, that property (3) is false for \( F \) for some \( s \in  \lbrack \varepsilon ,1) \) . Let \( {s}_{0} \in  \lbrack \varepsilon ,1) \) be the infimum of all \( s \in  \lbrack \varepsilon ,1) \) for which property (3) is false for \( F \) , i.e.,

\[
{s}_{0} \Doteq  \inf \{ s \in  \lbrack \varepsilon ,1) : F \smallsetminus  {C}_{ \clubsuit  }\left( s\right) \text{ is unbounded }\} .
\]

Then there exists a sequence \( {\left\{  {s}_{i}\right\}  }_{i \in  \mathbb{N}} \) with \( {s}_{i} \rightarrow  {s}_{0} \) such that \( F \smallsetminus  {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( {s}_{i}\right) \) is unbounded for all \( i \) . We shall obtain the contradiction from showing that \( F \smallsetminus  {C}_{4}\left( s\right) \) is bounded for any \( s \) sufficiently close to \( {s}_{0} \) .

For \( s \in  \lbrack 0,1) \) and \( \delta  > 0 \) define

\[
{C}_{\delta }\left( s\right)  \Doteq  \text{ the cone over the set }
\]

\[
\left\{  {\mathbf{R} \in  {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( s\right)  : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = 1,\operatorname{dist}\left( {\mathbf{R},\partial {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( s\right) }\right)  \geq  \delta }\right\}  ,
\]

which is a slightly smaller cone contained in \( {C}_{4}\left( s\right) \) (with \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\delta  \rightarrow  0}}{C}_{\delta }\left( s\right)  = \; \left. {{C}_{4}\left( s\right) }\right) \) . For \( \delta , h > 0 \) define

\[
{T}_{h}{C}_{\delta }\left( s\right)  \Doteq  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} \in  {C}_{\delta }\left( s\right) ,\operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \geq  h}\right\}  ,
\]

which is, as noted in [43], a 'truncated shifted cone'. We leave it to the reader to show that both \( {C}_{\delta }\left( s\right) \) and \( {T}_{h}{C}_{\delta }\left( s\right) \) are closed, convex, and \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant (convexity is the main issue). \( {}^{30} \)

(1) When \( \delta \) is sufficiently small, the cones \( {C}_{\delta }\left( s\right) \) are preserved by the ODE. For any \( s \in  \left( {0,1}\right) \) there exists \( {\delta }_{0} = {\delta }_{0}\left( s\right)  > 0 \) such that for all \( \delta  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{\delta }_{0}}\right\rbrack \) and \( \mathbf{R} \in  \partial {C}_{\delta }\left( s\right)  - \{ 0\} \) the vector \( Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone of \( {C}_{\delta }\left( s\right) \) .

This fact follows from

(i) \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\delta  \rightarrow  0}}\partial {C}_{\delta }\left( s\right)  = \partial {C}_{\Phi }\left( s\right) \) ,

(ii) the continuity of \( Q \) ,

(iii) our assumption that for \( \mathbf{R} \in  \partial {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( s\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} , Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) lies in the interior of tangent cone of \( {C}_{ \bullet  }\left( s\right) \) at \( \mathbf{R} \) , and

(iv) the fact that \( Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) is homogeneous of degree 2, i.e., \( Q\left( {c\mathbf{R}}\right)  = \; {c}^{2}Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) for all \( c \geq  0 \) (which addresses the issue of the noncompactness of the cones).

---

\( {}^{29} \) Note that we do not use property (2) here.

\( {}^{30} \) Note that the set \( \sum  \doteq  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} \in  {C}_{ \bullet  }\left( s\right)  : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = 1}\right\} \) is convex. To prove the convexity of \( {C}_{\delta }\left( s\right) \) , one just needs to show that

\[
\{ \mathbf{R} \in  \sum  : \operatorname{dist}\left( {\mathbf{R},\partial \sum }\right)  \geq  \delta \}
\]

is convex. The convexity of \( {T}_{h}{C}_{\delta }\left( s\right) \) also follows easily.

---

(2) Truncated shifted cones are preserved by the ODE. There exists \( \bar{h} \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) (in particular, for \( \bar{h} \) sufficiently large) such that the set

\[
{T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right)  = \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} \in  {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right\}   \cap  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \geq  \bar{h}\}
\]

is preserved by the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}\mathbf{R} = Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) for all \( \delta  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{\delta }_{0}\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right\rbrack \) .

First note that

\[
\partial \left( {{T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right)  \subset  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} \in  \partial {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right\}   \cup  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}\} .
\]

We have

\[
\operatorname{trace}Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = {\left| \operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \right| }^{2} \geq  \frac{4}{n}{\left( \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \right) }^{2} \geq  \frac{4}{n}{\bar{h}}^{2} > 0
\]

for \( \mathbf{R} \in  {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) (note that \( \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tr}\left( {\operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }\right) \) ).

Case (a). Hence for \( \mathbf{R} \) with \( \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h} \) the vector \( Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone of \( \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \geq  \bar{h}\} \) . This implies that for

\[
\mathbf{R} \in  \partial \left( {{T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right)  \smallsetminus  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} \in  \partial {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right\}   \subset  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}\} ,
\]

the vector \( Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone of \( {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) at \( \mathbf{R} \) , which is the half-space \( \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \geq  0\} \) .

Case (b). Now assume

\[
\mathbf{R} \in  \partial \left( {{T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}\}
\]

\[
\subset  \partial \left( {{T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right)  \cap  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} \in  \partial {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right\}
\]

so that in particular trace \( \left( \mathbf{R}\right)  > \bar{h} \) . In this case the tangent cone of \( {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) at \( \mathbf{R} \) is the same as the tangent cone of \( {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) at \( \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} \) (after shifting the vertex by \( \mathbf{I} \) ).

Let \( {\eta }_{0} \) be the infimum of the distance from \( Q\left( {\mathbf{R}}^{\prime }\right) \) to the boundary of the tangent cone of \( {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) among \( {\mathbf{R}}^{\prime } \in  \partial {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) with \( \operatorname{trace}\left( {\mathbf{R}}^{\prime }\right)  = 1 \) . Since by part (1), \( {\eta }_{0} > 0 \) , we have that the distance from \( Q\left( {\mathbf{R}}^{\prime }\right) \) to the boundary of the tangent cone of \( {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) grows quadratically; in particular, it is at least

(11.128)

\[
{\eta }_{0}{\left( \operatorname{trace}\left( {\mathbf{R}}^{\prime }\right) \right) }^{2} \geq  c{\eta }_{0}{\left| {\mathbf{R}}^{\prime }\right| }^{2}
\]

for all \( {\mathbf{R}}^{\prime } \in  \partial {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) , where \( c > 0 \) . For \( \mathbf{R} \in  \partial \left( {{T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right)  \cap  \{ \mathbf{R} : \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} \in \; \left. {\partial {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right\} \)

(i) let \( {d}_{1}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) be the distance of \( Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) to the boundary of the tangent cone of \( {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) at \( \mathbf{R} \) and

(ii) let \( {d}_{2}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) be the distance of \( Q\left( {\mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I}}\right) \) to the boundary of the tangent cone of \( {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) at \( \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} \) , so that by (11.128)

\[
{d}_{2}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \geq  c{\eta }_{0}{\left| \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I}\right| }^{2} \geq  \frac{1}{2}c{\eta }_{0}{\left| \mathbf{R}\right| }^{2}
\]

(with the last inequality holding for \( \bar{h} \) large enough). Next observe that

\[
\left| {Q\left( {\mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I}}\right)  - Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }\right|  = \left| {2\mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} + 2\mathbf{R}\# \mathbf{I} + \mathbf{I}\# \mathbf{I}}\right|
\]

\[
\leq  {A}_{1}\left| \mathbf{R}\right|
\]

for some constant \( {A}_{1} < \infty \) . Hence, by the triangle inequality and the above estimates,

\[
{d}_{1}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \geq  {d}_{2}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  - \left| {Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  - Q\left( {\mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I}}\right) }\right|
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{1}{2}c{\eta }_{0}{\left| \mathbf{R}\right| }^{2} - {A}_{1}\left| \mathbf{R}\right|
\]

so that \( {d}_{1}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  > 0 \) provided that \( \left| \mathbf{R}\right| \) is sufficiently large. Thus \( Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone of \( {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) at \( \mathbf{R} \) .

Case (c). Finally, if

\[
\mathbf{R} \in  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} \in  \partial {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right\}   \cap  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}\}  \subset  \partial \left( {{T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right) ,
\]

then by the arguments in proving Cases (a) and (b), it follows that \( Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone of \( {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) at \( \mathbf{R} \) .

By Cases (a),(b), and (c), we have shown that for all \( \mathbf{R} \in  \partial \left( {{T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right) \) , the vector \( Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone of \( {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) .

(3) Given any \( \bar{h} \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) , there exists \( \delta  > 0 \) (in particular, for \( \delta \) sufficiently small) such that the set \( {C}_{ \bullet  }\left( {s}_{0}\right)  \cap  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}}\right\} \) is contained in the interior of \( {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right)  \cap  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}}\right\} \) as subsets of the hyperplane \( \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}}\right\} \) . This is geometrically clear from considering the limit as \( \delta  \rightarrow  0 \) .

(4) By part (3), for \( \delta  > 0 \) sufficiently small and for \( s \) close enough to \( {s}_{0} \) , \( {C}_{ \bullet  }\left( s\right)  \cap  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}\} \) is contained in the interior of \( {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right)  \cap  \{ \mathbf{R} : \; \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}\} \) . We claim that by the definition of \( {s}_{0} \) , for \( \delta  > 0 \) sufficiently small there exists \( \bar{s} \in  \left\lbrack  {\varepsilon ,{s}_{0}}\right) \) (except when \( {s}_{0} = \varepsilon \) , where we let \( \bar{s} = {s}_{0} \) ) and \( k \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) large enough such that

(11.129)

\( F \cap  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = k\bar{h}\}  \subset  {C}_{\Phi }\left( \bar{s}\right)  \cap  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = k\bar{h}\}  \subset  k \cdot  {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) , \) that is,

\[
\frac{1}{k}F \cap  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}\}  \subset  {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( \bar{s}\right)  \cap  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}\}  \subset  {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) .
\]

(a) If \( {s}_{0} = \varepsilon  = \bar{s} \) , then the claim is clear since \( F \subset  {C}_{\Phi }\left( \varepsilon \right) \) .

(b) If \( {s}_{0} > \varepsilon \) , then \( F \smallsetminus  {C}_{\Phi }\left( \bar{s}\right) \) is compact for all \( \bar{s} \in  \left\lbrack  {\varepsilon ,{s}_{0}}\right) \) . Therefore, for each \( \bar{s} \in  \left\lbrack  {\varepsilon ,{s}_{0}}\right) \) , there exists \( {k}_{0} \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) such that the first inclusion in (11.129) holds for all \( k \geq  {k}_{0} \) .

(5) By part (4), for \( \delta  > 0 \) sufficiently small and \( k \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) large enough, the set

\[
{F}^{\prime } \Doteq  \left( {F \cap  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \leq  k\bar{h}}\right\}  }\right)  \cup  \left( {F \cap  k \cdot  {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right)
\]

is closed, convex, \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant, and preserved by the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}\mathbf{R} = Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) . In particular, the convexity of \( {F}^{\prime } \) follows from the inclusion (11.129). Now clearly \( {F}^{\prime } \subset  F \) . On the other hand, by the definition of \( F \) (in particular, its minimality), we have \( F \subset  {F}^{\prime } \) . Hence for \( \delta  > 0 \) sufficiently small and \( k \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) large enough,

\[
F = {F}^{\prime }\text{ . }
\]

(6) Since the set \( k \cdot  {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right)  \smallsetminus  {C}_{\delta /2}\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) is bounded, we have that the set \( {F}^{\prime } \smallsetminus  {C}_{\delta /2}\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) is bounded. On the other hand, clearly

\[
{F}^{\prime } \smallsetminus  {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( s\right)  \subset  {F}^{\prime } \smallsetminus  {C}_{\delta /2}\left( {s}_{0}\right)
\]

for any \( s \) close enough to \( {s}_{0} \) . Hence the set \( F \smallsetminus  {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( s\right)  = {F}^{\prime } \smallsetminus  {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( s\right) \) is bounded for any \( s \) close enough to \( {s}_{0} \) . This contradicts the definition of \( {s}_{0} \) since there exists a sequence \( {\left\{  {s}_{i}\right\}  }_{i \in  \mathbb{N}} \) with \( {s}_{i} \rightarrow  {s}_{0} \) such that \( F \smallsetminus  {C}_{ \bullet  }\left( {s}_{i}\right) \) is not bounded for all \( i \) .

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
(Justification of the canonical neighborhood assumption). Given any small \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , there exist decreasing sequences \( 0 < {\widetilde{r}}_{j} < \varepsilon ,{\kappa }_{j} > 0 \) , and \( 0 < {\widetilde{\delta }}_{j} < {\varepsilon }^{2}, j = 1,2,\cdots \) , with the following property. Define the positive function \( \widetilde{\delta }\left( t\right) \) on \( \lbrack 0, + \infty ) \) by \( \widetilde{\delta }\left( t\right)  = {\widetilde{\delta }}_{j} \) for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\left( {j - 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2}, j{\varepsilon }^{2}}\right) \) . Suppose there is a surgically modified solution, defined on \( \lbrack 0, T) \) with \( T <  + \infty \) , to the Ricci flow which satisfies the following:

(1) it starts on a compact orientable three-manifold with normalized initial metric, and

(2) it has only a finite number of surgeries such that each surgery at a time \( t \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) is a \( \delta \left( t\right) \) -cutoff surgery with

\[
0 < \delta \left( t\right)  \leq  \min \{ \widetilde{\delta }\left( t\right) ,\bar{\delta }\left( t\right) \} .
\]

Then on each time interval \( \left\lbrack  {\left( {j - 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2}, j{\varepsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack  \bigcap \lbrack 0, T), j = 1,2,\cdots \) , the solution satisfies the \( {\kappa }_{j} \) -noncollapsing condition on all scales less than \( \varepsilon \) and the canonical neighborhood assumption (with accuracy \( \varepsilon \) ) with \( r = {\widetilde{r}}_{j} \) .

Here and in the following, we call a (three-dimensional) surgically modified solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) ,0 \leq  t < T,\kappa \) -noncollapsed at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) on the scales less than \( \rho \) (for some \( \kappa  > 0,\rho  > 0 \) ) if it satisfies the following property: whenever \( r < \rho \) and

\[
\left| {{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {r}^{-2}
\]

for all those \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, r, - {r}^{2}}\right)  = \left\{  {\left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \mid  {x}^{\prime } \in  {B}_{{t}^{\prime }}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right) ,{t}^{\prime } \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {r}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) , for which the solution is defined, we have

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {r}^{3}.
\]

knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
The proof of the proposition is by induction: having constructed our sequences for \( 1 \leq  j \leq  m \) , we make one more step, defining \( {\widetilde{r}}_{m + 1} \) , \( {\kappa }_{m + 1},{\widetilde{\delta }}_{m + 1} \) , and redefining \( {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m} = {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m + 1} \) . In view of the previous lemma, we only need to define \( {\widetilde{r}}_{m + 1} \) and \( {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m + 1} \) .

In Theorem 7.1.1 we have obtained the canonical neighborhood structure for smooth solutions. When adapting the arguments in the proof of Theorem 7.1.1 to the present surgical solutions, we will encounter the new difficulty of how to take a limit for the surgically modified solutions. The idea to overcome the difficulty consists of two parts. The first part, due to Perelman [104], is to choose \( {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m} \) and \( {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m + 1} \) small enough to push the surgical regions to infinity in space. (This is the reason why we need to redefine \( {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m} = {\widetilde{\delta }}_{m + 1} \) .) The second part is to show that solutions are smooth on some small, but uniform, time intervals (on compact subsets) so that we can apply Hamilton's compactness theorem, since we only have curvature bounds; otherwise Shi's interior derivative estimate may not be applicable. In fact, the second part is more crucial. That is just concerned with the question of whether the surgery times accumulate or not. Our argument will use the canonical neighborhood characterization of the standard solution in Lemma 7.3.5.

We now start to prove the proposition by contradiction. Suppose for sequence of positive numbers \( {r}^{\alpha } \) and \( {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } \) , satisfying \( {r}^{\alpha } \rightarrow  0 \) as \( \alpha  \rightarrow  \infty \) and \( {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } \leq  \frac{1}{\alpha  \cdot  \beta }\left( { \rightarrow  0}\right) \) , there exist sequences of solutions \( {g}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) to the Ricci flow with surgery, where each of them has only a finite number of cutoff surgeries and has a compact orientable normalized three-manifold as initial data, so that the following two assertions hold:

(i) each \( \delta \) -cutoff at a time \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\left( {m - 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2},\left( {m + 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack \) satisfies \( \delta  \leq  {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } \) ; and

(ii) the solutions satisfy the statement of the proposition on \( \left\lbrack  {0, m{\varepsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack \) , but violate the canonical neighborhood assumption (with accuracy \( \varepsilon \) ) with \( r = {r}^{\alpha } \) on \( \left\lbrack  {m{\varepsilon }^{2},\left( {m + 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack \) .

For each solution \( {g}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) , we choose \( \bar{t} \) (depending on \( \alpha \) and \( \beta \) ) to be the nearly first time for which the canonical neighborhood assumption (with accuracy \( \varepsilon \) ) is violated. More precisely, we choose \( \bar{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {m{\varepsilon }^{2},\left( {m + 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack \) so that the canonical neighborhood assumption with \( r = {r}^{\alpha } \) and with accuracy parameter \( \varepsilon \) is violated at some \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) , however the canonical neighborhood assumption with accuracy parameter \( {2\varepsilon } \) holds on \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {m{\varepsilon }^{2},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) . After passing to subsequences, we may assume each \( {\widetilde{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } \) is less than the \( \widetilde{\delta } \) in Lemma 7.4.2 with \( r = {r}^{\alpha } \) when \( \alpha \) is fixed. Then by Lemma 7.4.2 we have uniform \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing on all scales less than \( \varepsilon \) on \( \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) with some \( \kappa  > 0 \) independent of \( \alpha ,\beta \) .

Slightly abusing notation, we will often drop the indices \( \alpha \) and \( \beta \) .

Let \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) be the rescaled solutions around \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) with factors \( R\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \left( { \geq  {r}^{-2} \rightarrow   + \infty }\right) \) and shift the times \( \bar{t} \) to zero. We hope to take a limit of the rescaled solutions for subsequences of \( \alpha ,\beta  \rightarrow  \infty \) and show the limit is an orientable ancient \( \kappa \) -solution, which will give the desired contradiction. We divide our arguments into the following six steps.

Step 1. Let \( \left( {y,\widehat{t}}\right) \) be a point on the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) with \( \widetilde{R}\left( {y,\widehat{t}}\right)  \leq  A \) (for some \( A \geq  1 \) ) and \( \widehat{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {-\left( {\bar{t} - \left( {m - 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{2}}\right) R\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) ,0}\right\rbrack \) . Then we have estimate

(7.4.14)

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {10A}
\]
